data.title: Launch HN: Augento (YC W25) – Fine-tune your agents with reinforcement learning
data.author: lmeierhoefer
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Augento平台的发布及其功能、市场定位、技术细节和潜在问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• lukasego对平台功能的介绍：平台移除了订阅连接的必要性，用户可以无摩擦地开始数据摄入，并继续欢迎用户反馈。
• zoogeny对平台服务模式的详细解析：认为该服务可以作为应用和OpenAI服务之间的代理，并详细描述了RL训练的整个流程，同时对该服务的市场定位和潜在客户进行了分析，提出RL的有效性是该业务成功的关键。
• resiros对奖励函数的关注：指出RL服务比单纯的微调服务更复杂，尤其是奖励函数的构建，建议改进文档和示例，并提出专注于一些常见的使用案例。
• jacobross对RL概念的兴趣和学习动机：虽然不是ML/DL背景，但对RL和高级学习非常感兴趣，并希望获得更多学习建议。
• HyprMusic对技术细节和成本的疑问：关注服务器冷启动时间和推理成本，并希望权重导出选项能早日实现。
• thebeardisred对Slack用户计费问题的抱怨：对Slack用户的计费方式表示不满。
• mogili对封闭源代码的反对：认为封闭源代码使得该平台不适合使用，并指出其似乎只适用于单代理工作流。
• filipeisho对模型托管自由的关注：希望能够自由选择模型的托管平台。
• georgeck对类似服务的比较：提到OpenPipe提供的Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)服务，并询问Augento解决方案的相似性。
• foundzen对训练样本数量的质疑：认为仅用20个训练样本就能提高LLM性能不现实，希望获得更多技术细节。
• serjester对大公司竞争的担忧：担心OpenAI等大公司最终会提供类似服务，使得小公司难以竞争。
• brap对SoTA模型API的疑问：认为当前SoTA专有模型已经提供微调API，大公司提供RL基于API只是时间问题。
• codingwagie对平台本质的批评：认为该平台只是围绕开源微调库的DevOps包装。
• esafak对模型下载功能的询问：询问用户是否可以下载微调后的模型。

补充讨论：
• 平台的服务模式和市场定位是讨论的核心，zoogeny和resiros提供了详细的分析和建议。
• 技术细节如奖励函数、训练样本数量、冷启动时间、推理成本等是用户关注的重点。
• 用户对模型托管自由、封闭源代码、计费问题等也有一定程度的关注和争议。
• 大公司竞争和SoTA模型API的发展是另一个值得注意的讨论点。

争议的焦点：
• 平台的独特性和市场竞争力，尤其是面对大公司可能提供类似服务时的生存能力。
• 技术实现细节如奖励函数的构建和训练样本数量的有效性。
• 用户对模型托管自由和封闭源代码的反对意见。

data.title: Go Optimization Guide
data.author: jedeusus
data.article_summary:
《Go应用性能优化系列》是一组技术文章，旨在帮助开发者编写更快速、高效的Go应用。该系列提供实用模式、真实案例及底层性能洞察，涵盖高吞吐量API、微服务和分布式系统的优化。虽然Go的性能调优选项不如C++或Rust多，但仍有许多方法能显著提升应用性能，包括内存重用、分配控制、高效网络及并发模式。

目前文章涵盖的性能模式包括：
1. 有效使用`sync.Pool`
2. 避免不必要的内存分配
3. 结构布局与内存对齐
4. 高效错误处理
5. 零成本抽象的接口
6. 就地排序与切片重用

后续将深入探讨高性能网络，包括`net/http`和`net.Conn`的高效使用、并发连接管理、性能调优及负载测试技术。该系列适合后端工程师、对延迟敏感系统的开发者及迁移到Go的团队。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中的内存管理、性能优化及相关工具和库的使用

不同观点：
• [nopurpose] 认为，减少GC时间的关键是避免长生命周期的分配，短生命周期的分配对GC时间影响很小。虽然所有分配都会触发GC，但优化GC标记阶段能带来更大的收益。
• [stouset] 对Go的类型系统提出批评，认为像`sync.Pool`这样的API因为使用`any`类型（以前的`interface{}`）而失去了类型安全的好处。同时建议增加一个可选的`Clear`回调来重置值。
• [kevmo314] 强调零拷贝代码的重要性及其在Go中的可行性，认为虽然需要仔细设计，但能显著减少内存分配和移动的时间。
• [__turbobrew__] 对将mmap称为“零拷贝”提出质疑，认为没有考虑到页故障和内存压力对性能的影响，这种误解曾在其他项目中导致问题。
• [donatj] 认为`sync.Pool`非常危险和易漏，建议除非万不得已，否则避免使用。
• [jrockway] 赞扬GOMEMLIMIT在控制内存使用和减少GC时间上的作用，特别是在容器化和CI环境中的实用性。
• [dennis-tra] 对编译器不能自动进行结构体字段对齐表示疑惑，认为这是可以自动化的事情。
• [parhamn] 询问是否有计划让像`sync`这样的包变得泛型。
• [jensneuse] 提醒注意`sync.Pool`可能导致的隐性内存使用增加，强调需要衡量实际收益而非仅依赖合成基准测试。

补充讨论：
• [roundup] 提供了一些关于Go优化的资源链接，并希望这些内容能作为工具集成到IDE中以帮助记忆和应用。
• [nikolayasdf123] 对当前Go优化技巧的内容组织表示赞赏，并建议创建一个社区驱动的平台来共享优化建议和研究。
• [kunley] 对示例中默认使用32位架构表示疑惑，质疑其现实适用性。
• [_345] 询问是否有类似Python 3的优化资源。

争议焦点：
• 对`sync.Pool`的使用存在争议，一方面认为其危险且易漏，另一方面则强调其在性能优化中的潜在价值。
• 对零拷贝和mmap的定义和实际效果存在不同理解，反映了在实际应用中的复杂性和误解风险。

43539585.article_content:
Patterns and Techniques for Writing High-Performance Applications with Go
¶
The
Go App Optimization Series
is a collection of technical articles aimed at helping developers write faster, more efficient Go applications. Whether you're building high-throughput APIs, microservices, or distributed systems, this series offers practical patterns, real-world use cases, and low-level performance insights to guide your optimization efforts.
While Go doesn’t expose as many knobs for performance tuning as languages like C++ or Rust, it still provides
plenty of opportunities
to make your applications significantly faster. From memory reuse and allocation control to efficient networking and concurrency patterns, Go offers a pragmatic set of tools for writing high-performance code.
We focus on
concrete techniques
with
mesurable impact
you can apply immediately—covering everything from core language features to advanced networking strategies.
What’s Covered So Far
¶
Common Go Patterns for Performance
¶
In this first article, we explore a curated set of high-impact performance patterns every Go developer should know:
Using
sync.Pool
effectively
Avoiding unnecessary allocations
Struct layout and memory alignment
Efficient error handling
Zero-cost abstractions with interfaces
In-place sorting and slices reuse
Each pattern is grounded in practical use cases, with benchmarks and examples you can copy into your own codebase.
What’s Coming Next
¶
High-Performance Networking in Go
¶
In our upcoming deep dive into networking, we'll focus on building high-throughput network services with Go’s standard library and beyond. This includes:
Efficient use of
net/http
and
net.Conn
Managing large volumes of concurrent connections
Performance tuning with epoll/kqueue and
GOMAXPROCS
Load testing techniques and bottleneck diagnostics
TBD...
We'll also explore when to drop down to lower-level libraries like
fasthttp
, and how to balance performance with maintainability.
Who This Is For
¶
This series is ideal for:
Backend engineers optimizing Go services in production
Developers working on latency-sensitive systems
Teams migrating to Go and building performance-critical paths
Anyone curious about Go’s performance model and trade-offs
Stay tuned—more articles, code samples, and tools are on the way. You can bookmark this page to follow the series as it evolves.

data.title: Canoeing on the Danube
data.author: karagenit
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了在多瑙河上划独木舟的建议和常见问题。多瑙河是欧洲第二长河，夏季常有人从德国至匈牙利进行划舟活动，还有每年一度的"多瑙河国际巡回赛"（TID），提供详细的行程和地图。划舟者可使用BIKELINE出版的多瑙河自行车道地图，但最后300公里需额外地图。划舟无需许可，但各国规则不同，如塞尔维亚需挂国旗，奥地利在水闸处需穿救生衣。多瑙河上有超过100个水坝，大多在德奥境内，TID提供详细行程和港口信息。遇到水坝时，通常需搬运独木舟，有些地方有滑道可利用。在塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚的Djerdap I和II水坝可能遇到阻碍，需耐心沟通以通过。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：丹麦河（Danube）及其相关冒险活动、文化和地理特点

不同观点：
• rdtsc：介绍了丹麦河三角洲是欧洲第二大三角洲，并提到当地有俄罗斯旧礼仪派（Lipovans）的村庄，还提到已故的罗马尼亚著名皮划艇运动员Ivan Patzaichin来自该地区。
• axelfontaine：分享了自己骑行整个丹麦河的经历，从德国黑森林的Brigach和Breg河源一直骑到罗马尼亚的三角洲，并邀请其他人提问。
• aredox：提供了关于丹麦河上的航行和划船冒险的更多阅读材料，强调了该河流的文化重要性。
• konradha：对80公里/天的划船距离表示惊讶，并提到自己在柏林北部最多只能完成30公里/天，还质疑"Shengan"是否为英式拼写。
• nicbou：表达了对这类详尽且信息丰富的页面的喜爱，认为它不同于如今通过谷歌搜索找到的大多数内容，并且非常小众。
• gaussiandistro：提供了更多关于丹麦河上划船冒险的阅读资源。
• MomsAVoxell：住在维也纳，经常划皮艇（不是划船）在Donau河上，认为这是一个非常有趣且充满冒险的河流，尤其是在春夏季，可以逃离城市的喧嚣。
• drpixie：提供了与主题类似的阅读材料，提到《The Unlikely Voyage of Jack de...》。
• avh02：建议如果想要更短且轻松的体验，可以去捷克南部的Vltava河漂流，那里基本上是一个懒人河，有很多营地。
• mobilio：住在保加利亚的丹麦河边，提到每年都有TID（丹麦国际旅游）活动。
• nickfromseattle：作为美国人，曾在贝尔格莱德住在距离丹麦河100米的地方，生活了4年，目标是乘船穿越欧洲，希望船能比皮划艇大些。
• Gys：质疑划船通常是否顺流而下，因为有人一天能划80公里，并提到文章未说明河流的流向和水流速度。

补充讨论：
• 地理和文化背景：评论中提到了丹麦河的地理特征、文化重要性以及当地居民（如俄罗斯旧礼仪派村庄）。
• 个人经历分享：多位评论者分享了自己在丹麦河及其支流上的划船、骑行和漂流经历，提供了实际的体验和建议。
• 争议焦点：konradha对80公里/天的划船距离表示怀疑，并质疑"Shengan"的拼写问题；Gys则对河流流向和水流速度提出了疑问。

43516117.article_content:
Travel and Lifestyle Writer with a focus on camping and the outdoors
Canoeing on the Danube: Advice & FAQs
CANOEING ON THE DANUBE
The Danube is Europe's second longest river and undergoes dramatic changes throughout its course. Though big, it is paddled fairly regularly each summer, particularly from Germany through to Hungary. There is also the organised
Tour International Danube
each year, a huge regatta where a large group paddle the entire length of the river. Their itinerary is extremely useful, outlining distances per day, the locations of locks and more. The 2017 itinerary can be found
here
. Below are probably just a few of your questions, so if you want to know more just get in touch through our
contact page
.
What maps did you use to canoe the Danube?
For the Danube we used the BIKELINE maps for the DANUBE CYCLE PATH (donauradweg) which come in a range of languages and can be ordered online. These maps cover the entire river and are a fantastic scale providing great detail. The maps also act as a concise guide book giving tid-bits of historic information along route. You need nothing more than these maps with the exception of the final 300kms of the Danube where the cycle path leaves the river in Romania. If you plan to canoe this section it is important to get another, up to date, map since the river here is awash with islands and difficult to navigate. To find such maps we suggest you contact
Tour International Danube
(TID)
who apparently provide specific maps for this section.
Do you need a river permit to canoe on the Danube?
No. The Danube is an international waterway and permits are not required. There are certain rules for individual countries that should be adhered to however. In Serbia national flags
must be flown (or an equivalent sticker on the canoe). In Austria life jackets must be worn at locks or dams (we strongly suggest you wear lifejackets the entire time, however. We did). In Germany you should have a boat name and address clearly marked on the vessel and should be affiliated with a canoeing body (for us membership of the British Canoe Union (BCU)).
Where are there dams on the river?
The Danube has more than 100 Dams with most in Germany and Austria, quickly petering out thereafter.  All of these dams and locks are well signposted and some have buoys that lead you to the river bank. The
Tour International Danube
publishes its annual itinerary which features all there camp points, along with all obstacles and locks including what bank you should pull in for portage (L or R) and what distance marker the Portage should begin. This information is accurate and definitely worth using, it can be found
here
on their 2017 PDF file.
N.B. On
TID
s itinerary for 15.07.17 in location named 'Cunovo' the description is to portage on the right bank to the old Danube river bed. This complicated section of the itinerary is deceiving, since there are really two options on the right hand side: You can go 'far right' or to a large dam that is on the right hand side but does not go all the way to the river-bank. It is for this dam you want to head and, once closer, you will find sign posts to help you with the portage. In short: at 1852 go right but head for the dam not for the river-bank, here there are signs for canoes.
How do I get around the dams?
There are a two ways around the locks. At most you must carry or wheel your canoe. There will be a ramp, or a series of steps which you can use. Sometimes there will be a trolley waiting there for you and you can wheel your canoe around the dam, and down to a similar dock on the far side of the dam. If there is no trolley, there might be one on the far side, so it could be worth a walk around to see.
On some dams there are shoots that you can slide down in your canoe. Sometimes you will see a bell and rope on the bank near one of these banks or a lever to pull. By ringing the bell you alert the control tower who will open the gate for you. Once this has lowered and the green light shows you can plummet down the ramp. If, like us, you find you are not canoeing during tourist season there may be no one there to operate the ramp. For this you can either carry around or (be cheeky) and go down the slide anyway even though theres not much water on it. but be careful because you don't want to get stuck!
The two locks in Serbia/Romania marked as Djerdap I and II are the only places you may have problems. The lock keepers do not want to deal with canoes and there is no sign posted set up here. We got shooed away from the lock on either side of the dam but eventually convinced the Romanian side to let us in with a cruise ship and go down in the lock. At the second we chatted and were slowed by countless members of authority but were eventually allowed to walk around and place our canoe back in the river on the other side. With these locks prepare for a long wait and a lot of talking, ultimately you have a right to be allowed passed.

43516117.article_summary: 本文介绍了在多瑙河上划独木舟的建议和常见问题。多瑙河是欧洲第二长河，夏季常有人从德国至匈牙利进行划舟活动，还有每年一度的"多瑙河国际巡回赛"（TID），提供详细的行程和地图。划舟者可使用BIKELINE出版的多瑙河自行车道地图，但最后300公里需额外地图。划舟无需许可，但各国规则不同，如塞尔维亚需挂国旗，奥地利在水闸处需穿救生衣。多瑙河上有超过100个水坝，大多在德奥境内，TID提供详细行程和港口信息。遇到水坝时，通常需搬运独木舟，有些地方有滑道可利用。在塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚的Djerdap I和II水坝可能遇到阻碍，需耐心沟通以通过。

43505340.article_content:
Jussi Koskela tells us the secret behind the game’s unique feeling of flying.
This is a complicated time for ski jumping in Norway. Interest has been declining for years, with plenty of negative press, and it all peaked recently with the disappointing revelations of widespread suit cheating among Norwegian jumpers. But perhaps we can use this rough patch to reminisce about truly great ski jumping experiences — experiences that, of course, took place in front of a screen.
Deluxe Ski Jump developer Jussi Koskela’s ski-jumping toy that you can see at the Finnish Museum of Games (Photo: Jussi Koskela)
There have been several games that have given us varying degrees of that wonderful feeling of lift. Growing up, I mostly stared into a screen powered by MS-DOS, and I’m guessing that most of us DOS folks have at some point played The Games: Winter Challenge. It offered a variety of winter sports activities, but let’s be honest — ski jumping was the only fun one. It was incredibly frustrating, though, that it was impossible to land jumps where you actually timed the take-off perfectly.
Back when the New Year’s competition in Garmisch-Partenkirchen felt more important than New Year’s Eve, I was thrilled to discover a little game called Four Hills by Jukka Hakosalo. It let me take part in the whole Four Hills Tournament, competing against legends like Bredesen and Goldberger. The game was very simple, but sometimes it doesn’t take much to be entertained.
But everything changed the year we discovered Deluxe Ski Jump. It was the game we’d been waiting for all along. At last, the ultimate ski jumping game had arrived. We had a chat with the man who gave us this gift more than 25 years ago.
First of all—who are you?
I’m Jussi Koskela, a 45-year-old solo game developer from Finland, and I’ve been working on the Deluxe Ski Jump games since 1999.
Jussi Koskela at the Pixel Heaven 2024 in Warsaw together with DSJ2 players. (Photo: Jussi Koskela)
How did you get started with game development?
I started making little games already as a child. When I was 9, I wrote my first «game», where the goal was to kill a giant spider by swinging a sword at the right time. You just had to press F1 once to win the game.
Later, my games grew in complexity and size little by little. I sold my first game when I was 12, to a friend who was 7. I think he was mostly interested in the source code…
Can you tell us about your first commercial game, Fatal Fumes?
Fatal Fumes is a top-down racing game I developed as a hobby project in my teens. My brother helped me a bit with the physics, and a friend contributed the music. We also built the tracks together.
For me, Fatal Fumes was mostly a learning project, since it was my first full-scale game. Programming was very different back then because there were no ready-made libraries for sound or graphics, so you had to code everything from scratch. The biggest challenge was getting the game to run smoothly at 70 FPS. I also struggled a bit with implementing CPU opponents who could drive well enough.
Of course, we dreamed of big sales, but Fatal Fumes never became a commercial success. Still, I was very proud that the game’s demo was included on the cover disks of PC Gamer and PC Format magazines in the UK.
Fatal Fumes. Image: Mobygames.
My friends and I played Slicks ’n’ Slide a lot, and it was definitely an inspiration for our racing game. Fatal Fumes aimed to be something similar, but with larger tracks that spanned multiple screens. The charm of Slicks ’n’ Slide was always the multiplayer mode on a shared keyboard, but that didn’t work so well in Fatal Fumes, since I never managed to implement proper split-screen.
How did you end up making a new ski jumping simulator?
I had been experimenting with side-scrolling graphics that gave an effective 3D feel. It was originally meant for a platformer, but at some point, it reminded me of a ski jumping hill. I felt that other ski jumping games at the time had very simplistic physics and didn’t really capture the feeling of flight, so I decided to give it a go myself.
What were the biggest challenges you faced?
The biggest challenge was time. I only had three months off after high school before starting military service, and I finished the game just one day before I had to report in!
Technically, the hardest part was making the hills and environments look believable using my «fake» 3D graphics. The actual simulation part was mostly basic high school physics. I never took any programming courses in high school, so experience and code snippets from earlier projects were invaluable.
The most important factor in the game’s success was making the jumping feel fantastic—and I spent a lot of time on that. I think the biggest innovation was how the mouse controls were mapped to the jumper’s movements. It made players respond with their whole bodies, as if they were ski jumpers themselves.
Original Deluxe Ski Jump. Image: Mobygames.

data.title: Excitable cells
data.author: johannes_ne
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲解了心脏折返性心律失常的形成和维持条件。心肌细胞（心肌细胞）激活时会去极化，引发连锁反应。正常情况下，心脏由窦房结控制，称为窦性心律。如果出现一个非响应区域（如心肌梗死后疤痕组织），去极化波可以绕行形成自我维持的回路，导致折返性心动过速，例如房室结折返性心动过速或室性心动过速。这些心律失常可能无害，也可能致命，如室性纤颤。要引发折返性心律，去极化波需绕过非响应区域，且不同路径的不应期长短不一。通过电击（除颤）或巧妙 timing 的异位搏动可恢复窦性心律。纤颤则是另一种复杂的心律失常，心肌细胞无序激活。

43504940.article_content:
I wrote this post to answer some of the questions, I had as a medical student, when I first learned about cardiac arrhythmias. Mainly, what are the conditions required to initiate and maintain a
reentrant arrhythmia
? That is, a state where the heart muscles are continuously activated by a self-sustaining loop, independent of the normal pace-making system. These arrhythmias can be benign, as with
AV-nodal reentry tachycardia (AVNRT)
; a common, and usually harmless, cause of palpitations in young people. Or they can be deadly, as with
ventricular fibrillation
.
Heart muscle cells (cardiomyocytes) have some interesting properties. When they are activated, they
depolarize
. Depolarization causes the cell to contract, but also activates neighboring cells, setting of a chain reaction.
For the following demonstrations, we use i highly simplified model of heart. Below is a grid of simulated cardiomyocytes, each ready to activate their neighboring cells. They all start in a
resting state
, ready to be
activated
.
Activated cells are black. After a short moment, they become inactive and
refractory
. Refractory cells cannot be activated. In the simulation, refractory cells go from dark gray to light gray, until they have regained their resting state, and are ready for a new activation.
👆️ Click/tap anywhere in the box below to activate a cell.
Notice, that the activation is not entirely symmetric and predictable. To give the simulation a more organic feel, I added a bit of randomness to the activation of cells. Each cell is activated with a higher probability the more of its four neighbors are active (33% chance if one neighbor is active, 100% chance when 3 or 4 neighbors are active).
Pacemaker cells
Sinus rhythm. From
ECGpedia
.
Another interesting property of cardiomyocytes is their
automaticity
; cardiomyocytes spontaneously activate if they are not stimulated by a neighboring cells for a period. Cells in the
sinoatrial node
(sinus node) in the right atrium have the fastest rate of spontaneous activation, and thus activate the remaining heart, making the sinus node the heart’s pacemaker.
In the following simulation, a cluster of cells in the top left corner act as pacemaker cells.
👆️ Move the slider below the simulation to change the rate of spontaneous depolarization (heart rate).
When the spontaneous depolarization of the sinus node determines the heart rate, the heart is said to be in
sinus rhythm
, which is the normal (physiological) activation path of the heart. If the sinus node paces the heart at a rate faster than 100 beats per minute, the rhythm is called
sinus tachycardia
. Sinus tachycardia (together with increased stroke volume) increases the flow of blood from the heart, and is the physiological response to exercise.
Reentry tachycardia
Ventricular tachycardia. From
Ecgpedia
.
In reentry tachycardia, the heart is not paced by the sinus node, but instead from a group of cells that have formed a circuit, where a wave of depolarization can loop around and stimulate itself over and over. This requires a non-responsive area among the cells (an area that cannot be activated), so a circuit can form around it.
In the simulation below, the red cells are non-responsive (dead). They could represent scar tissue after a
myocardial infarction
—
a common cause of ventricular tachycardia
. Or the simulation could illustrate
atrial flutter
, where a reentrant loop can form around the tricuspid valve.
👆️ To stop the reentrant tachycardia, shock the cardiac cells by pressing the “⚡️ Defibrillate!” button.
⚡️ Defibrillate!
After defibrillation, the system is in sinus rhythm. The pacemaker cells were always there, but were suppressed by the reentrant loop.
The simulation above illustrates how a reentrant loop can sustain itself around a dead area, but how does it start in the first place?
👆️ You can try to click/tap on the simulation above to set of an ectopic beat (a depolarization starting outside the sinus node), but you will not be able to initiate a reentrant loop again.
How does a reentrant loop start?
To initiate a reentrant loop, the wave of depolarization must be traveling only one way around the dead area. Otherwise the two waves traveling in opposite will just eliminate each other when they meet at the other side. However, if one pathway has cells with a
longer refractory period
, a wave of depolarization can arrive exactly when one pathway is ready to depolarize, while the other is still refractory.
In the simulation below, cells in the lower left corner have a longer refractory period.

Regent Craft, a developer specializing in all-electric seagliders based in Rhode Island, has completed its initial contract with the U.S. Marine Corps Warfighting Lab (MCWL).

High-speed, radar-proof electric seagliders

This will involve demonstrations relevant to specific defense operations, a crucial aspect as military needs evolve.
Tom Huntley, Vice President of Government Relations and Defense at Regent, expressed pride in continuing collaboration with the Marine Corps.
He highlighted the role of Regent’s seagliders in meeting national security requirements, specifically in logistics operations that face challenges in contested maritime environments.
The advantages of seagliders are particularly noteworthy for defense operations, where speed and efficiency can determine the success of missions.
The Viceroy seaglider can soar up to 180 mph over approximately 180 miles.
One of the standout features of sea gliders is their ability to take off and land on water.
This capability eliminates reliance on traditional runways, which can be vulnerable in conflict situations.

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了AWS如何利用形式化及半形式化方法确保系统正确性，以提供高可靠性服务。AWS主要使用TLA+语言进行形式化验证，帮助在开发早期发现并修复潜在错误，同时支持性能优化。然而，由于TLA+学习曲线陡峭，AWS引入了更易用的P编程语言，用于建模和验证分布式系统。P语言已在多个AWS核心产品中应用，如S3存储服务的强一致性迁移。此外，AWS开发了PObserve工具，用于在测试和生产环境中验证分布式系统的正确性。这种系统化的正确性实践显著提升了开发效率，并确保服务的高可靠性和成本效益。

Systems Correctness Practices at AWS
Leveraging Formal and Semi-formal Methods
Marc Brooker and Ankush Desai
AWS (Amazon Web Services) strives to deliver reliable services that customers can trust completely. This demands maintaining the highest standards of security, durability, integrity, and availability—with systems correctness serving as the cornerstone for achieving these priorities. An April 2015 paper published in
Communications of the ACM
, titled "How Amazon Web Services Uses Formal Methods," highlighted the approach for ensuring the correctness of critical services that have since become among the most widely used by AWS customers.
21
Central to this approach was TLA+,
14
a formal specification language developed by Leslie Lamport. Our experience at AWS with TLA+ revealed two significant advantages of applying formal methods in practice. First, we could identify and eliminate subtle bugs early in development—bugs that would have eluded traditional approaches like testing. Second, we gained the deep understanding and confidence needed to implement aggressive performance optimizations while maintaining systems correctness.
Moreover, 15 years ago, AWS's software testing practice relied primarily on build-time unit testing, often against mocks, and limited deployment-time integration testing. Since then, we have significantly evolved our correctness practices, integrating both formal and semi-formal approaches into the development process. As AWS has grown, formal methods have become increasingly valuable—not only for ensuring correctness but also for performance improvements, particularly in verifying the correctness of both low- and high-level optimizations. This systematic approach toward systems correctness has become a force multiplier at AWS's scale, enabling faster development cycles through improved developer velocity while delivering more cost-effective services to customers.
This article surveys the portfolio of formal methods used across AWS to deliver complex services with high confidence in its correctness. We consider an umbrella definition of formal methods that encompasses these rigorous techniques—from traditional formal approaches such as theorem proving,
7,10
deductive verification,
18
and model checking
8,14
to more lightweight semi-formal approaches such as property-based testing,
6,19
fuzzing,
9
and runtime monitoring.
11
The P Programming Language
As the use of formal methods was expanded beyond the initial teams at AWS in the early 2010s, we discovered that many engineers struggled to learn and become productive with TLA+. This difficulty seemed to stem from TLA+'s defining feature: It is a high-level, abstract language that more closely resembles mathematics than the imperative programming languages most developers are familiar with. While this mathematical nature is a significant strength of TLA+, and we continue to agree with Lamport's views on the benefits of mathematical thinking,
15
we also sought a language that would allow us to model check (and later prove) key aspects of systems designs while being more approachable to programmers.
We found this balance in the P programming language.
8
P is a state-machine-based language for modeling and analysis of distributed systems. Using P, developers model their system designs as communicating state machines, a mental model familiar to Amazon's developer population, most of whom develop systems based on microservices and SOAs (service-oriented architectures). P has been developed at AWS since 2019 and is maintained as a strategic open-source project.
22
Teams across AWS that build some of its flagship products—from storage (e.g., Amazon S3, EBS), to databases (e.g., Amazon DynamoDB, MemoryDB, Aurora), to compute (e.g., EC2, IoT)—have been using P to reason about the correctness of their system designs.
For example, P was used in migrating S3 (Simple Storage Service) from eventual to strong read-after-write consistency.
1
A key component of S3 is its index subsystem, an object metadata store that enables fast data lookups. To achieve strong consistency, the S3 team had to make several nontrivial changes to the S3 index protocol stack.
25
Because these changes were difficult to get right at S3 scale, and the team wanted to deliver strong consistency with high confidence in correctness, they used P to formally model and validate the protocol design. P helped eliminate several design-level bugs early in the development process and allowed the team to deliver risky optimizations with confidence, as they could be validated using model checking.
In 2023, the P team at AWS built PObserve, which provides a new tool for validating the correctness of distributed systems both during testing and in production. With PObserve, we take structured logs from the execution of distributed systems and validate post-hoc that they match behaviors allowed by the formal P specific

Bletchley Park code breaker Betty Webb has died at the age of 101
A decorated World War Two code breaker who spent her youth deciphering enemy messages at Bletchley Park has died at the age of 101.
Charlotte "Betty" Webb MBE - who was among the last surviving Bletchley code breakers - died on Monday night, the Women's Royal Army Corps Association confirmed.
Mrs Webb, from Wythall in Worcestershire, joined operations at the Buckinghamshire base at the age of 18, later going on to help with Japanese codes at The Pentagon in the US. She was awarded France's highest honour - the Légion d'Honneur - in 2021.
The Women's Royal Army Corps Association described Mrs Webb as a woman who "inspired women in the Army for decades".
Bletchley Park Trust CEO Iain Standen said Mrs Webb will not only be remembered for her work but "also for her efforts to ensure that the story of what she and her colleagues achieved is not forgotten."
"Betty's passion for preserving the history and legacy of Bletchley Park has undoubtedly inspired many people to engage with the story and visit the site," he said in a statement.
Tributes to Mrs Webb have begun to be posted on social media, including one from historian and author Dr Tessa Dunlop who said she was with her in her final hours.
Describing Mrs Webb as "the very best", she said on X: "She is one of the most remarkable woman I have ever known."
Mrs Webb told the BBC in 2020 that she had "never heard of Bletchley", Britain's wartime code-breaking centre, before starting work there as a member of the ATS, the Auxiliary Territorial Service.
She had been studying at a college near Shrewsbury, Shropshire, when she volunteered as she said she and others on the course felt they "ought to be serving our country rather than just making sausage rolls".
Her mother had taught her to speak German as a child and ahead of her posting remembered being "taken into the mansion [at Bletchley] to read the Official Secrets Act".
"I realised that from then on there was no way that I was going to be able to tell even my parents where I was and what I was doing until 1975 [when restrictions were lifted]," she recalled.
She would tell the family with whom she lodged that she was a secretary.
Listen on BBC Sounds: Mrs Webb went to work at Bletchley Park when she was 18
When the War ended in Europe in May of 1945, she went to work at the Pentagon after spending four years at Bletchley, which with its analysis of German communications had served as a vital cog in the Allies' war machine.
At the Pentagon she would paraphrase and transcribe already-decoded Japanese messages. She said she was the only member of the ATS to be sent to Washington, describing it as a "tremendous honour".
Mrs Webb, in 2020, recalled she had had no idea the Americans planned to end the conflict by dropping atomic weapon on Japanese cities, describing the weapons' power as "utterly awful"
After the Allies' final victory, it took Mrs Webb several months to organise return passage to the UK, where she worked as a secretary at a school in Shropshire.
The head teacher there had also worked at Bletchley so knew of her professionalism, whereas other would-be employers, she recalled, were left stumped by her being unable to explain - due to secrecy requirements - her previous duties.
More than half a century later, in 2021, Mrs Webb was one of 6,000 British citizens to receive the Légion d'Honneur, following a decision by President François Hollande in 2014 to recognise British veterans who helped liberate France.
PA Media
Betty Webb, seen in the front row in a red suit, was invited to the Coronation
In 2023, she and her niece were among 2,200 people from 203 countries invited to Westminster Abbey to see King Charles III's coronation.
The same year she celebrated her 100th birthday at Bletchley Park with a party.
She and her guests were treated to a fly-past by a Lancaster bomber. She said at the time: "It was for me - it's unbelievable isn't it? Little me."

data.title: Donkey Kong champion wins defamation case against Australian YouTuber Karl Jobst
data.author: throw7
data.article_summary: 澳大利亚YouTuber卡尔·乔布斯特（Karl Jobst）因在2021年一段YouTube视频中诽谤美国游戏玩家、唐克金刚（Donkey Kong）冠军比利·米切尔（Billy Mitchell），被布里斯班地方法院判赔35万澳元及利息和诉讼费。乔布斯特在视频中指控米切尔作弊，并错误地将他与另一位YouTuber阿波罗传奇（Apollo Legend）的自杀联系起来，暗示米切尔逼死了他。尽管米切尔此前因作弊指控被取消了多项游戏纪录，但法官认为乔布斯特未充分调查即发布视频，存在“轻率无视真相”的行为，严重损害了米切尔的名誉并导致其痛苦。乔布斯特否认指控但被判败诉，需支付30万澳元非经济损失赔偿和5万澳元加重损害赔偿。法院未裁定米切尔是否在游戏中作弊。

Donkey Kong champion wins defamation case against Australian YouTuber Karl Jobst
Queenslander ordered to pay $350,000 plus interest and costs as judge finds his video about American gamer Billy Mitchell was ‘recklessly’ based on false claim

A professional YouTuber in Queensland has been ordered to pay $350,000 plus interest and costs to the former world record score holder for Donkey Kong, after the Brisbane district court found the YouTuber had defamed him “recklessly” with false claims of a link between a lawsuit and another YouTuber’s suicide.
William “Billy” Mitchell, an American gamer who had held world records in Donkey Kong and Pac-Man going back to 1982, as recognised by the Guinness World Records and the video game database Twin Galaxies, brought the case against Karl Jobst, seeking $400,000 in general damages and $50,000 in aggravated damages.
Jobst, who makes videos about “speed running” (finishing games as fast as possible), as well as gaming records and cheating in games, made a number of allegations against Mitchell in a 2021 YouTube video. He accused Mitchell of cheating, and “pursuing unmeritorious litigation” against others who had also accused him of cheating, the court judgment stated.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s breaking news email
The court heard Mitchell was accused in 2017 of cheating in his Donkey Kong world records by using emulation software instead of original arcade hardware. Twin Galaxies investigated the allegation, and subsequently removed Mitchell’s scores and banned him from participating in its competitions.
The Guinness World Records disqualified Mitchell as a holder of all his records – in both Donkey Kong and Pac-Man – after the Twin Galaxies decision.
The judgment stated that Jobst’s 2021 video also linked the December 2020 suicide of another YouTuber, Apollo Legend, to “stress arising from [his] settlement” with Mitchell, and wrongly asserted that Apollo Legend had to pay Mitchell “a large sum of money”.
‘There’s no stress’: gamers go offline in retro console revival
Read more
The judgment noted multiple versions of the video were published, with the allegations removed or addressed, before Jobst issued a retraction video in July 2021, two months after the original. The first video was viewed by more than 500,000 people, including 200,000 in Australia, the court heard.
Judge Ken Barlow found Jobst had made five defamatory imputations about Mitchell, including that Mitchell had required Apollo Legend pay him a large sum of money and thus implying he “in essence, hounded Apollo Legend to death”.
Barlow found this was “based on a fallacy” – and that Jobst, in not making further inquiries before publishing the video, had been “recklessly indifferent” to if it was true.

data.author: ww520
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Zig语言中的拓扑排序库TopoSort。该库主要用于对依赖图进行拓扑排序，具有以下功能：构建依赖图、执行拓扑排序、生成无依赖子集以支持并行处理、检测循环依赖并报告循环。它支持不同类型的节点，并提供了安装、使用、内存管理、配置和基准测试的详细说明。

### 主要特点：
1. **安装**：通过`zig fetch`命令添加库到项目中。
2. **使用**：导入库并初始化，添加依赖数据，执行排序，检查循环依赖。
3. **内存管理**：节点按值传递和存储，简单类型直接复制，切片和指针类型不复制内存。
4. **配置**：`TopoSort.init()`函数接受可选配置，如`verbose`标志和`max_range`属性。
5. **并行处理**：生成无依赖子集，支持并行处理节点。

该库通过配置`max_range`属性，使用简单数据结构提升性能，排序速度可提高3至4倍。

TopoSort - Topological Sort on Dependency Graph
TopoSort is a highly efficient Zig library for performing topological sort on dependency graph.  This small library is packed with the following features:
Building dependency graph from dependency data.
Performing topological sort on the dependency graph.
Generating dependence-free subsets for parallel processing.
Cycle detection and cycle reporting.
Support different node types.

主要讨论点：Myst游戏的技术实现、体验方式（原版 vs 现代版）、以及相关技术工具和改进建议。

不同观点：
• [deater] 认为在制作Apple II版本的Myst I时，手工生成游戏数据结构图表非常繁琐，并好奇是否可以通过自动化工具简化这个过程。这表明早期开发过程中手工操作较多，开发者在思考自动化可能性。

• [anon84873628] 提到想体验Myst但错过了其巅峰时期，询问是否通过模拟器体验原版更好，还是玩现代重制版。这反映了玩家在原版与重制版之间的选择困惑，关注点在于游戏体验的原汁原味与技术改进的平衡。

• [gwbas1c] 反驳了Myst提供“自由探索”的说法，认为Myst的自由度主要体现在没有敌人和难度过高的关卡，而3D游戏在当时已经可以自由移动和查看任何东西。他将Myst的探索体验与现代游戏（如《塞尔达传说：旷野之息》）进行了对比，指出Myst的自由度实际上是相对有限的。

补充讨论：
• [hoten] 分享了为《Silent Hill 2》制作的类似图表工具，并提供了源码链接，这扩展了讨论到其他游戏的技术实现。

• [immibis] 指出了文章中某个段落描述与图标实际显示不符的问题，属于技术细节的修正。

• [gcanyon] 提供了第二篇文章的链接，丰富了讨论的资源。

• [NBJack] 询问图表的原始数据是否可以获取，表现出对技术细节和数据使用的兴趣。

• [doublerabbit] 分享了一篇关于消除Myst 4加载时间的技术文章，扩展了讨论到游戏性能优化方面。

• [guerrilla] 建议制作一个使用实际场景图片的交互式图表，提出了对用户体验改进的期望。

• [alex1138] 以幽默方式表达了对“真实链接书”的期待，属于对未来技术突破的畅想。

争议焦点：Myst的“自由探索”程度。一方认为Myst提供了相对自由的探索体验，另一方则认为这种自由是相对有限的，与同时期的3D游戏相比并不突出。

• [gwbas1c] 反驳了Myst提供“自由探索”的说法，认为Myst的自由度主要体现在没有敌人和难度过高的关卡，而3D游戏在当时已经可以自由移动和查看任何东西。他将Myst的探索体验与现代游戏（如《塞尔达传说：旷野之息》）进行了对比，指出Myst的自由度实际上是相对有限的。

补充讨论：
• [hoten] 分享了为《Silent Hill 2》制作的类似图表工具，并提供了源码链接，这扩展了讨论到其他游戏的技术实现。

• [immibis] 指出了文章中某个段落描述与图标实际显示不符的问题，属于技术细节的修正。

• [gcanyon] 提供了第二篇文章的链接，丰富了讨论的资源。

• [NBJack] 询问图表的原始数据是否可以获取，表现出对技术细节和数据使用的兴趣。

• [doublerabbit] 分享了一篇关于消除Myst 4加载时间的技术文章，扩展了讨论到游戏性能优化方面。

• [guerrilla] 建议制作一个使用实际场景图片的交互式图表，提出了对用户体验改进的期望。

• [alex1138] 以幽默方式表达了对“真实链接书”的期待，属于对未来技术突破的畅想。

争议焦点：Myst的“自由探索”程度。一方认为Myst提供了相对自由的探索体验，另一方则认为这种自由是相对有限的，与同时期的3D游戏相比并不突出。

data.title: RubyUI (Former PhlexUI): Ruby Gem for RubyUI Components
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: RubyUI 是一个开源的 Ruby gem，提供可复制粘贴的 UI 组件，旨在加速开发过程。它并非传统的组件库，而是通过生成或复制组件代码供开发者自由定制使用。其特点包括高速性能（基于 Phlex，比 Rails ERB 模板快 12 倍）、精美且可高度自定义的 UI、低依赖性以及易于复用。安装简便，通过命令行即可完成，并提供详细文档和组件生成器。RubyUI 强调开发者对组件设计的完全控制，适合构建个性化的组件库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Phlex项目及其在Ruby和前端开发中的应用和评价

不同观点：
• GenericCanadian：认为Phlex让前端开发变得有趣，尤其赞赏其通过使用纯Ruby和私有方法作为部分模板来改进UI重构的能力，并分享了自己的项目实例。
• anonygler：对Phlex持批评态度，认为其性能声称不实，且对垃圾收集器压力大、调试困难，主张前端应更多使用JS/JSX，而不是类似Phlex的方案。
• ajmaia：支持Phlex，表示在新的Rails 8项目中使用预发布版本效果很好。
• budu：赞赏Phlex的功能，但指出组件命名空间问题，认为需要手动处理组件名称。
• alexmccain6：对Phlex在大型应用中的可扩展性及内存使用、调试方面的潜在问题表示关注。
• drumpkid：对Phlex的进展表示赞赏，但对声称的性能提升缺乏可见的基准测试表示疑虑。
• jspash：对Phlex使用PascalCase命名方式表示不解，质疑其是否为了吸引React开发者。
• daviding：对Phlex方法持保留态度，尝试使用Date Picker组件时遇到问题。
• cbeltrao、luispimenta、desireco42：简单表达了对Phlex项目的赞赏和兴趣。
• dzonga：询问是否有实际的大型项目使用了Phlex。
• justinko：幽默地表示如果不支持复制/粘贴HTML则不感兴趣。
• ramesh31：赞赏Phlex组件的外观，但不确定谁会使用及为何使用。

补充讨论：
- Phlex的性能声称及其基准测试的透明性和可信度是一个争议点，尤其是anonygler和drumpkid对此提出质疑。
- Phlex的组件命名和DSL设计（PascalCase）引发了jspash的疑问，反映出对Ruby开发者习惯的考虑。
- 关于Phlex在实际项目中的应用和可扩展性是另一个讨论焦点，ajmaia和alexmccain6分享了使用经验和关注点，而dzonga则直接询问实际案例。
- justinko和ramesh31的观点则反映了部分开发者对Phlex实用性和目标用户群体的困惑。

RubyUI (former PhlexUI) 🚀
Beautifully designed components that you can copy and paste into your apps. Accessible. Customizable. Open Source.
This is NOT a component library. It's a collection of re-usable components that you can generate or copy and paste into your apps.
Pick the components you need. Copy and paste the code into your project and customize to your needs. The code is yours.
Use this as a reference to build your own component libraries.
Key Features:
Built for Speed
⚡: RubyUI leverages Phlex, which is up to 12x faster than traditional Rails ERB templates.
Stunning UI
🎨: Design beautiful, streamlined, and customizable UIs that sell your app effortlessly.
Stay Organized
📁: Keep your UI components well-organized and easy to manage.
Customer-Centric UX
🧑‍💼: Create memorable app experiences for your users.
Completely Customizable
🔧: Full control over the design of all components.
Minimal Dependencies
🍃: Uses custom-built Stimulus.js controllers to keep your app lean.
Reuse with Ease
♻️: Build components once and use them seamlessly across your project.
How to Use:
Find the perfect component
🔍: Browse live-embedded components on our documentation page.
Copy the snippet
📋: Easily copy code snippets for quick implementation.
Make it yours
🎨: Customize components using Tailwind utility classes to fit your specific needs.
Installation 🚀
1. Install the gem
bundle add ruby_ui --group development --require
false
or add it to your Gemfile:
gem
"ruby_ui"
,
group
:
:development
,
require
:
false
2. Run the installer:
bin/rails g ruby_ui:install
3. Done! 🎉
You can generate your components using
ruby_ui:component
generator.
bin/rails g ruby_ui:component Accordion
Documentation 📖
Visit
https://rubyui.com/docs/introduction
to view the full documentation, including:
Detailed component guides
Themes
Lookbook
Getting started guide
Speed Comparison 🏎️
RubyUI, powered by Phlex, outperforms alternative methods:
Phlex: Baseline 🏁
ViewComponent: ~1.5x slower 🚙
ERB Templates: ~5x slower 🐢
See the original
view layers benchmark
by @KonnorRogers and its
variations
.

data.title: Launch HN: ASim (YC S21) – Mobile app that generates mobile apps
data.author: dli123
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"aSim"项目的功能、技术实现、未来发展及相关问题

不同观点：
• [ncr100] 对项目的音频功能进行了测试，发现可以通过"Enable Sound API/Access"开启声音功能，并分享了一个将英语转为摩尔斯电码并播放声音的链接。同时，提醒长时间播放摩尔斯电码可能无法停止，存在用户体验问题。

• [zkid18] 对项目的未来发展表示乐观，认为技术开发不再是瓶颈，真正的挑战在于如何进行有效的分发和定位。他预测类似aSim的功能将融入当前的媒体平台，比如TikTok如果推出AI应用商店，可能会优先采用低摩擦、高留存的应用（如AI增强视频功能）。他还提到平台方和创作者的双赢局面，并设想通过创新的方式绕过应用商店的30%抽成。

• [bambax] 遇到了技术问题，反复看到“Oops! Simulation failed”和“Try Fixing”的错误提示，且错误信息不完整，导致无法有效调试。此外，对'Agent'和'Genius'这两个术语的含义表示困惑。

• [aaurelions] 猜测aSim是基于a0.dev和Expo技术实现的。

• [realprimoh] 对项目的未来 monetization（变现）模式表示关注，询问开发者如何计划实现盈利。

• [ddxv] 关心生成的“应用”是托管在自己的Google Play账户下还是仅限于aSim内部。

• [leonhard] 遇到了验证码接收问题，无法在英国号码上收到验证码，影响体验。

• [pzo] 提到当前多个类似的移动应用生成器，并列举了一些竞品，指出它们大多使用Expo技术来生成React Native应用。

• [swyx] 对后端技术实现表示关注，询问开发者如何处理后端需求，是否使用Firebase或Supabase等技术，并询问这些技术的优缺点。

• [sirjaz] 希望项目能扩展到桌面应用，询问开发者是否有相关计划。

• [purple-leafy] 幽默地表示希望有一个“生成移动应用的移动应用生成器”，表达了对更多类似工具的需求。

• [asim] 自嘲自己作为AI应用生成器的开发者，最终可能与自己的作品竞争工作机会。

• [compootr] 认为这是一个四月愚人节的玩笑。

• [lukaskf] 对项目表示赞赏，认为这是他见过的消费者/应用/游戏领域中较为酷炫的AI应用案例之一。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：部分用户如[bambax]遇到了技术问题，错误信息不完整且无法有效调试，影响了使用体验。
• 技术实现：多个用户如[aaurelions]、[pzo]和[swyx]对项目的技术实现表示关注，讨论了使用Expo、React Native以及后端技术选择等问题。
• 未来发展：[zkid18]和[sirjaz]对项目的未来发展方向提出了自己的看法，包括市场定位、变现模式以及扩展到桌面应用的可能性。
• 幽默评论：[asim]和[compootr]以幽默的方式表达了对项目的看法，分别提到了与自己作品竞争和工作机会的问题，以及对项目真实性的调侃。

data.author: bavarianbob

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：npm和相关网站中包含"camel"的路径被阻止的问题及其原因和影响

不同观点：
• Recursing：指出了在npm和其他相关网站上，包含"camel"的路径被触发阻止的问题，并提供了问题追踪链接和解决状态更新。
• tom_usher：认为问题源于Cloudflare的WAF规则集的变更，特别是与'Apache Camel - Remote Code Execution'相关的规则，并提到可以自行覆盖该规则来解决问题。
• pvg：批评Cloudflare的WAF产品以往也有类似问题，指出其偶尔会引发一些意外的故障，影响互联网服务的正常运行。
• nwalters512：提到npm官方已经确认了该事件，并提供了状态更新链接。
• miyuru：认为将WAF外包是双刃剑，并质疑像GitHub或Microsoft这样的大公司为何不自己组建WAF团队。
• klysm：认为将安全作为附加产品购买往往会带来此类问题。
• mplanchard：表示对该问题的发生感到困惑，并感谢有人提出此问题。
• drusepth：询问该问题是否也导致了unpkg网站的频繁上下波动。

补充讨论：
• 问题被官方确认并已解决，具体见状态更新链接。
• 讨论中涉及对Cloudflare WAF产品可靠性的批评及其对互联网服务的影响。
• 对大公司依赖外包安全产品（如WAF）的策略提出质疑。
• 一些用户对该问题引发的连锁反应（如unpkg网站的波动）表示关注。

• miyuru：认为将WAF外包是双刃剑，并质疑像GitHub或Microsoft这样的大公司为何不自己组建WAF团队。
• klysm：认为将安全作为附加产品购买往往会带来此类问题。
• mplanchard：表示对该问题的发生感到困惑，并感谢有人提出此问题。
• drusepth：询问该问题是否也导致了unpkg网站的频繁上下波动。

补充讨论：
• 问题被官方确认并已解决，具体见状态更新链接。
• 讨论中涉及对Cloudflare WAF产品可靠性的批评及其对互联网服务的影响。
• 对大公司依赖外包安全产品（如WAF）的策略提出质疑。
• 一些用户对该问题引发的连锁反应（如unpkg网站的波动）表示关注。

Debts, Tech and Otherwise
While people debate the validity of "tech debt", others are asking, "What other sorts of 'debt' do we have in software development and delivery?"
09 March 2025
tl;dr
A colleague of mine, Scott Porad (CTO, VP Engineering) posted on LinkedIn, asking, "What are all the other kinds of debt like tech debt?" He listed out a few, then asked for others to weigh in, and the list grew... kinda long. And interesting. And made me think about the metaphor more deeply.
His list
included financial debt (the OG), Product debt (gaps in the product that impact revenue or lead to support costs), Ops Debt (manual processes performed by the operations team because the software doesn't support the processes), Process Debt (valuable steps of the software development process that are skipped causing quality or velocity issues), and Org Debt (key roles that are not staffed that cause quality or velocity issues).
He then asked others to weigh in with their favorites, and the answers poured in. Many (I won't list them all--partly because I want you to read the original post!) were interesting, and I think they fall into a variety of different categories:
Technological.
Whether it's the data, the UX/Design, the backend, or even the choice to over-depend on open-source without "giving back". Documentation falls in here, too.
Procedural.
What processes are being done by hand that cost the team time, money, or energy? What sorts of things are being hidden by a "lightweight process" focus (a la "agile") because companies are afraid to institute a process, lest they be called "not agile"?
Mental.
What assumptions were made that turned out to be wrong? What assumptions were right "back then" but no longer hold? Is the organization chasing the right problems? What knowledge is missing from the people that need to know?
Cultural.
Any group of humans forms a culture, but is that culture serving the business, or holding it back?
Talent.
A few of the responses mentioned "youth" or "experience" debt, as in a lack of investment into junior talent, or a refusal to recognize the value of experienced veteran talent on the team. Likewise, having "not enough" in raw terms, e.g., understaffed teams.
Support.
This is a more nebulous catch-all category but includes things like "marketing" (neglecting marketing practices over time, leading to damaged brand and customer relationship) or "legal" (failure to recognize the legal and/or regulatory necessities, bringing the company into legal jeopardy).
Again, I encourage readers to go check out Scott's original post. It was fascinating how much of it just poured out in the comments, and the wide-ranging nature of the responses.
Which got me thinking: Are these really "debts"? Or, more to the point, are they bad?
Debt: A Metaphor
If we go back to the original definition of "tech debt", if I remember correctly, I first heard it from Mike Clark back on the NFJS tour in the late 2000s, but
Wikipedia tells me
that Ward Cunningham first coined the term in 1992 as a metaphor to explain to his boss how making short-term decisions can boomerang and create problems over time, and therefore investment was needed to refactor the code. In particular, the point of the analogy was that "While technical debt can accelerate development in the short term, it may increase future costs and complexity if left unresolved." The official Wikipedia definition of "Technical debt", by the way, is this: "the implied cost of additional work in the future resulting from choosing an expedient solution over a more robust one."
Ward put it like this:
"Shipping first time code is like going into debt. A little debt speeds development so long as it is paid back promptly with a rewrite... The danger occurs when the debt is not repaid. Every minute spent on not-quite-right code counts as interest on that debt. Entire engineering organizations can be brought to a stand-still under the debt load of an unconsolidated implementation, object-oriented or otherwise."
Martin Fowler later
wandered into this arena
, too, pointing out that debt is sometimes taken on deliberately (a car loan, a mortgage) for good purposes, and sometimes it's accrued accidentally (credit card debt) because of poor planning or execution. He likened it to a
quadrant
along two axes: reckless vs prudent, deliberate vs inadvertent:
In almost all of the "pain" cases of debt, re

data.author: naveen_k
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为WattWise的终端CLI工具，用于实时监控和优化工作站的电力消耗。该工具通过TP-Link Kasa智能插座获取电力数据，并在终端中展示电流功耗和历史消耗图表，支持颜色编码以区分使用水平。WattWise支持自动根据分时电价调整CPU和GPU性能，以节省电力开支。其功能包括实时功耗监控、历史数据图表、自动节流控制以及与Home Assistant集成。尽管智能插座测量精度有限，但对实际使用监控已足够。工具提供直接安装和Docker部署选项，并使用PI控制器动态调整系统性能，以适应电力费率和系统负载变化。该工具简化了高性能计算中的电力管理，帮助用户在性能和能耗之间找到平衡。

CLI dashboard showing real-time and historical power draw readings from a Kasa smart plug
The Challenge: Performance vs. Power Costs
High-performance computing often means high electricity bills, especially in regions with time-of-use pricing. Finding the balance between computational power and energy efficiency becomes critical when running resource-intensive workloads.
Current Workstation Specs
CPUs: Dual EPYC 7C13 (base 2GHz, boost 3.7GHz) - 128 cores total (256 threads)
Motherboard: Gigabyte MZ72-HB2
RAM: 512GB DDR4
GPUs: 2x A4000 16GB
GPUs: 2x 4090 48GB (Upcoming)
Storage: 10TB NVMe
PSU: Coolmaster 1600W Platinum
Understanding Power Usage
I have been setting up a workstation for off-loading compute-intensive LLM workflows from my desktop. The build includes dual Epyc CPUs with plans to add 4 GPUs for up to 128GB VRAM to run multiple agents in parallel. A key constraint was ensuring the system could run comfortably on a standard household 120V outlet.
Since I already use smart plugs throughout my home, I added one to monitor the workstation’s power consumption. However, checking power statistics using the kasa phone app or Home Assistant dashboard proved cumbersome, especially when I already maintain a terminal window with monitoring tools like htop, nvtop, and nload in a 2×2 grid on my secondary display.
TP-link Kasa EP25 Smart Plug
Building a Terminal-Based Solution
After sketching a simple wireframe for what I wanted: a clean, terminal-based UI that would display power consumption data already being collected by my Home Assistant instance through the TP-Link integration. After getting the data access sorted, I spent some time with ‘Claude 3.7 Sonnet Thinking’ iterating on the CLI structure and features.
The result: WattWise, a lightweight CLI tool that pulls power usage data from smart plugs (either directly or through Home Assistant) and presents it in a clean, information-dense dashboard right in the terminal.
WattWise Demo
Key Features
Monitoring Features
Real-time power monitoring with wattage and current display
Color-coded power values (green for low usage, yellow for medium, red for high)
Historical consumption charts directly in the terminal
While smart plug measurements aren’t lab-grade (typically ±1-3% accuracy), they’re more than sufficient for practical usage monitoring
Power Management Features
Automatic CPU/GPU throttling based on time-of-use electricity pricing
Configurable power thresholds and performance profiles
Simple configuration through an interactive setup process
Deployment Options
Direct installation from source code
Docker support for containerized deployment
Connection options for both direct Kasa smart plug access and Home Assistant integration
Dynamic Power Management
Since my utility provider uses Time of Use (ToU) pricing. Over the years, I’ve built various home automations to minimize electricity usage during peak hours. With my workstation potentially drawing up to 1400W at full load, it made sense to add automatic CPU and GPU throttling during expensive rate periods.
Power Optimizer: System architecture
My testing showed that reducing CPU frequency from 3700MHz to 1500MHz saved approximately 225W under load on my specific setup, though results will vary by hardware. The power optimizer service dynamically adjusts clock speeds based on:
System load (from os.getloadavg())
Current power consumption (from the smart plug)
Time of day (to account for ToU periods)
Power Optimizer: ToU adaption chart
Adaptive Performance Control
Initially, I explored a full PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controller, but a simpler PI (Proportional-Integral) approach proved more suitable for power management.
The PI controller focuses on two key aspects:
Proportional (P) term: Provides immediate, proportional response to current errors
Integral (I) term: Accumulates past errors to eliminate long-term steady-state deviations
By removing the Derivative term, we:
Simplify the control logic
Reduce computational overhead
Maintain smooth performance transitions
Avoid potential over-optimization from the derivative calculation
For systems with gradual state changes like power management, the derivative term often introduces unnecessary complexity without meaningful benefits.
The controller dynamically adapts system parameters by considering:
Current system utilization (CPU/GPU load)
Instantaneous power consumption
Time-of-use electricity rate periods
This approach ensures energy-efficient transitions without the complexity of a full PID implementation.
Power Optimizer: Control flow (with PID)
Implementation and Limitations
Terminal Interface
The dashboard design is simple with:
A large, easy-to-read current wattage display
Color-coded elements based on consumption thresholds
Real-time updates with configurable refresh intervals
Historical graph using Unicode block characters for compatibility across terminals
Data Sources
The tool supports two main data sources:
Direct Kasa Connection

• gorbypark：正在进行一个基于西班牙电价API的独立项目，目标是创建一个超低功耗设备，每天唤醒一次检查电价，以实现非技术用户的自动化。
• gitpusher：赞赏该项目，认为尽管有批评，但作为黑客项目非常出色，CLI工具的外观很棒。
• throwaway3231：支持“race-to-idle”策略，认为快速完成任务即使功耗高也通常更节能。
• Havoc：认为家庭发电在大多数国家不具经济竞争力，仅在学习或处理高度机密信息时有意义。
• mythrwy：幽默地建议在节流时播放歌曲片段。
• gtirloni：询问具体节省的美元金额。
• whalesalad：建议使用大容量UPS或电源银行，在电价便宜时充电，电价高时使用。
• ajsnigrutin：质疑为何不使用简单的cronjob根据时间切换性能和节能模式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于节流PC或调整任务执行时间是否能真正节省能源或电费，部分观点认为只是降低功率而不减少任务量可能不会降低总能耗。
• 项目实现的技术细节如代码实现、设备选择和具体节省效果也受到关注。
• 不同用户根据自己的技术背景和项目需求提出了各种实现方案，如使用API、创建独立设备或简单的时间调度方案。

data.author: AnhTho_FR
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对订阅和支付模式的看法，以及对Kagi支付系统的具体讨论。

不同观点：
• **joshstrange**：对新的支付和订阅模式表示兴趣，特别是John Siracusa的Hyperspace提供的多种支付选项（按月、按年、终身等）。他提到自己不反对订阅，但希望有自动取消的选项，避免长期绑定，尤其是对不常使用的应用。他以Adobe为例，表示如果有“1个月无续订”选项，他可能会继续使用Photoshop。

• **siquick**：分享个人经验，表示Kagi是他唯一从未想过要取消的订阅服务，暗示对该服务的满意度很高。

• **7373737373**：对Kagi使用Yandex表示担忧，指出部分数据和资金可能流向俄罗斯，隐含对隐私和政治因素的顾虑。

• **leejoramo**：提到ProVUE’s Panorama X数据库应用的“不用不付费”计划，提供另一种支付模式的例子，支持joshstrange对灵活支付选项的需求。

• **Rebelgecko**：质疑Kagi用户是否构成比其他搜索引擎用户更具社区性的群体，暗示对Kagi自称的“社区”概念持怀疑态度。

• **superultra**：关注潜在的客户服务问题，特别是用户在长时间未使用后再次使用时被收费的情况，质疑用户是否会记得自己曾注册过，并指出Kagi团队可能未充分考虑这些边缘情况。

• **rmholt**：对Kagi的商业模式可持续性提出疑问，担心其是否会像OpenAI一样转向盈利模式，暗示对Kagi长期商业策略的关注。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对Kagi的看法存在分歧，有人非常满意（siquick），有人则担心数据隐私和商业模式（7373737373，rmholt）。
• 对灵活支付选项的需求是一个重要讨论点，joshstrange和leejoramo都提到希望有更灵活的支付和订阅模式，以适应不常使用或短期使用的应用。
• 争议的焦点包括Kagi自称的“社区”概念是否真实以及其商业模式的可持续性（Rebelgecko，rmholt）。

data.title: Dave Täht has died
data.author: mhandley
data.article_summary: 戴夫·塔特（Dave Täht）不幸去世，他是一位杰出人物，以开发FQ-CoDel和CAKE算法而闻名，这些技术有效解决了网络延迟和连接质量问题，造福了全球数百万人。他的工作改善了视频通话的可靠性，使许多人能够通过网络获得医疗和与家人保持联系。戴夫的贡献全部为免费和开源，帮助了包括Starlink在内的许多项目解决延迟问题，并支持了发展中国家的互联网接入。他的工作对技术界产生了深远影响，激励了无数人。他的朋友和同事们深切缅怀他，铭记他对世界的巨大贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：悼念Dave Täht，讨论他的贡献及其影响

不同观点：
• 一些评论表达了对Dave Täht的悼念之情，强调他对bufferbloat问题的长期努力和贡献，尽管大多数人并不了解这个问题。例如，[petedoyle]和[dlenski]都提到Dave对网络问题的深入研究和勤奋态度，以及他对技术领域的榜样作用。
• [bzg]和[zoobab]分享了与Dave的个人互动经历，强调了他的热情和对全球连接的重视，以及他在技术会议和社区活动中的参与。
• [i_am_a_peasant]强调Dave对他个人职业发展的影响，特别是在低层次网络工作上的启发和指导。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了Dave的具体技术贡献，如[zitterbewegung]提到他在Goto Chicago会议上的演讲和他对TCP模型的使用，以及[lxgr]提到Dave在OpenWrt和bufferbloat方面的工作如何影响了他的学习。
• [schoen]和[raggi]讨论了Dave在技术项目中的合作和挑战，显示了他在技术社区中的活跃角色以及他的不同方法如何带来积极影响。
• [pabs3]提出了关于专有软件和GPL违规对Dave工作推广的限制问题，这是一个关于开源和专有系统之间冲突的实际问题。
• [askonomm]对Dave的姓氏感到好奇，试图探讨他的潜在爱沙尼亚背景，这增加了对Dave个人身份的兴趣。
• [sinak]引用了Vint Cerf对Dave的评价，进一步强调了Dave在互联网技术领域的重大影响和贡献。

争议焦点：
• 争议并不明显，但[pabs3]提出的关于专有和开源系统之间的矛盾可能引发进一步讨论，即如何在更广泛的范围内推广像Dave Täht这样的技术贡献。

整体来看，评论主要集中在Dave Täht的技术贡献、个人影响力和对他去世的悼念。他的工作不仅在技术层面产生了深远影响，也在个人层面上激励了许多人。

43550098.article_content:
In loving memory of Dave Täht
04/01/2025
We’re devastated to report that Dave Täht has passed away.
Dave was an amazing man, helping the world with FQ-CoDel and CAKE, fighting bufferbloat and trying to make the world a better place. Always willing to help, and without him – LibreQoS (and the other QoE solutions out there) wouldn’t exist.
Dave was an inspiration, and we all miss him. We’re reaching out to family and close friends to see if there’s anything we can do to help.
Dave was an inspiration to us. Dave’s contributions to Linux, FQ-CoDel, and CAKE improved internet connectivity around the world for millions of people. Because of him, millions of people now have access to reliable video calls – and in turn, access to loved ones, healthcare, and community. One of Robert’s ISP customers is a kind paraplegic woman who lives in a far-flung rural Colonia around El Paso, Texas. Her reliable access to her doctors through telemedicine, and to her family through FaceTime, was only made possible because of his algorithms. There are millions of cases like hers, where Dave’s contributions have silently enabled human connection and safety. Everything Dave contributed to the world of technology was free and open source, for the betterment of humanity.
Dave is the reason that Starlink was able to tackle its latency issues – enabling a generation of young entrepreneurs across the developing world, such as these young folks pictured in the Phillipines, to start their own ISPs to expand internet access to their communities. Dave started work on FQ-CoDel in part because of his own journey working to expand internet access in Nicaragua, so we know he saw that his work had come full-circle and helped so many.
We’re incredibly grateful to have Dave as our friend, mentor, and as someone who continuously inspired us – showing us that we could do better for each other in the world, and leverage technology to make that happen. He will be dearly missed.
PS:
Dave is forever in our hearts and souls, in our routers and… in production.
https://github.com/LibreQoE/LibreQoS/pull/684
We will miss you so much, Dave.
– Robert, Herbert, and Frank with LibreQoS

data.title: Generate autounattend.xml files for Windows 10/11
data.author: nixass
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过各种方法和工具优化Windows系统的安装和配置，以避免不必要的软件和优化系统性能。

不同观点：
• [chem83] 建议通过安装英文（世界）语言版来避免自动安装多余的软件，并提到在首次启动后可以改回首选语言，但需重启以防止多余软件安装。
• [juujian] 对Windows系统需要各种变通方法表示不满，认为这很令人惊讶。
• [atVelocet] 提供了多项详细的技术建议，包括使用LTSC或IoT/Enterprise版本、使用NTLite工具、配置GroupPolicies、安装防火墙和NextDNS、禁用某些安全功能和微代码加载等。
• [j1elo] 列举了一些希望通过配置文件自动应用的Windows设置，并表示希望有一个.reg文件生成网站来实现这一点。
• [cwillu] 提到无法关闭粘滞键快捷方式的问题，表示在新机器上经常误触。
• [_JamesA_] 分享了使用生成器在VMWare Workstation中部署Windows 11 Enterprise虚拟机的积极体验。
• [CSDude] 表示喜欢使用固态颜色背景，特别是Windows 95的背景颜色。
• [teknopaul] 希望有一个类似的工具用于.deb文件，认为这会很有帮助。
• [nullwarp] 表示几周前非常需要这样的工具，认为这个工具很不错。
• [theandrewbailey] 分享了使用unattend.xml文件将C:\Users目录放在硬盘上而其他部分放在SSD上的经验，尽管文档警告不要这样做。
• [kalev] 询问是否可以通过此方法禁用autopilot/mdm。
• [nicman23] 请求添加企业IoT版本，并对工具表示赞赏。
• [7bit] 认为使用Windows ADK才是专业做法，并认为这个工具是完全无用的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于使用各种工具和方法的必要性和有效性。例如，[atVelocet] 和 [7bit] 对工具的选择有不同的看法，前者推荐NTLite，后者认为Windows ADK才是专业选择。
• 用户对具体设置和功能的需求不同，例如关闭粘滞键快捷方式、配置特定背景颜色等，显示出个性化配置的重要性。
• 经验分享中，[theandrewbailey] 的做法与官方文档建议相悖，但其个人经验表明这种方法是可行的，增加了讨论的深度。

data.title: Show HN: Qwen-2.5-32B is now the best open source OCR model
data.author: themanmaran
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Omni OCR Benchmark，一个用于比较多种大型多模态模型（如gpt-4o）在OCR和数据提取（尤其是JSON提取）方面性能的基准工具。其目标是发布一个全面的OCR准确性基准，涵盖传统OCR提供商和多模态语言模型。基准数据集和方法均为开源，并鼓励扩展以包含更多提供商。

基准评估主要关注JSON提取准确性和文本相似度（通过Levenshtein距离测量）。评估过程包括文档OCR和提取，结果保存为JSON格式。用户可以通过克隆项目、安装依赖、准备数据并运行基准测试来使用该工具，结果将保存在指定文件中。

支持的模型包括闭源和开源LLM，以及云OCR提供商。基准仪表板可用于查看每次测试的结果。该项目依据MIT许可证发布。

主要讨论点：Qwen新发布的模型及其在视觉语言任务（尤其是OCR和图像处理）中的表现

Omni OCR Benchmark
A benchmarking tool that compares OCR and data extraction capabilities of different large multimodal models such as gpt-4o, evaluating both text and json extraction accuracy. The goal of this benchmark is to publish a comprehensive benchmark of OCRaccuracy across traditional OCR providers and multimodal Language Models. The evaluation dataset and methodologies are all Open Source, and we encourage expanding this benchmark to encompass any additional providers.
Open Source LLM Benchmark Results (Mar 2025)
|
Dataset
Benchmark Results (Feb 2025)
|
Dataset
Methodology
The primary goal is to evaluate JSON extraction from documents. To evaluate this, the Omni benchmark runs
Document ⇒ OCR ⇒ Extraction
. Measuring how well a model can OCR a page, and return that content in a format that an LLM can parse.
Evaluation Metrics
JSON accuracy
We use a modified
json-diff
to identify differences between predicted and ground truth JSON objects. You can review the
evaluation/json.ts
file to see the exact implementation. Accuracy is calculated as:
$$\text{Accuracy} = 1 - \frac{\text{number of difference fields}}{\text{total fields}}$$
Text similarity
While the primary benchmark metric is JSON accuracy, we have included
levenshtein distance
as a measurement of text similarity between extracted and ground truth text.
Lower distance indicates higher similarity. Note this scoring method heavily penalizes accurate text that does not conform to the exact layout of the ground truth data.
In the example below, an LLM could decode both blocks of text without any issue. All the information is 100% accurate, but slight rearrangements of the header text (address, phone number, etc.) result in a large difference on edit distance scoring.
Running the benchmark
Clone the repo and install dependencies:
npm install
Prepare your test data
For local data, add individual files to the
data
folder.
To pull from a DB, add
DATABASE_URL
in your
.env
Copy the
models.example.yaml
file to
models.yaml
. Set up API keys in
.env
for the models you want to test. Check out the
supported models
here.
Run the benchmark:
npm run benchmark
Results will be saved in the
results/<timestamp>/results.json
file.
Supported models
To enable specific models, create a
models.yaml
file in the
src
directory. Check out the
models.example.yaml
file for the required variables.

43549072.article_summary:
本文介绍了Omni OCR Benchmark，一个用于比较多种大型多模态模型（如gpt-4o）在OCR和数据提取（尤其是JSON提取）方面性能的基准工具。其目标是发布一个全面的OCR准确性基准，涵盖传统OCR提供商和多模态语言模型。基准数据集和方法均为开源，并鼓励扩展以包含更多提供商。

基准评估主要关注JSON提取准确性和文本相似度（通过Levenshtein距离测量）。评估过程包括文档OCR和提取，结果保存为JSON格式。用户可以通过克隆项目、安装依赖、准备数据并运行基准测试来使用该工具，结果将保存在指定文件中。

支持的模型包括闭源和开源LLM，以及云OCR提供商。基准仪表板可用于查看每次测试的结果。该项目依据MIT许可证发布。

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了硅胶如何成为广泛使用的防潮材料。硅胶颗粒内部充满微小孔隙，具有极大的表面积，能够通过毛细凝结吸附高达自重40%的水蒸气，因此被广泛用于食品、电子产品和衣物等各类包装中，以防止潮湿和霉变。虽然每个硅胶包的吸水能力有限，但供应商提供计算工具帮助确定所需硅胶量。此外，硅胶还被用于艺术品展示柜中，以维持稳定的湿度环境。硅胶因其高效的吸湿性能，已成为现代包装中不可或缺的一部分。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：硅胶包的实际效果、用途、再利用方法及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• IAmBroom认为，99%的硅胶包在化妆品中使用，实际效果有限。如果硅胶包在非密封容器或包装中存放，它们在出厂前就已经吸满水分，失去效果。许多人误解了硅胶包的功能，以为它们可以无限吸收湿气。
• Civitello以幽默方式提到一种糖果，外形和包装像硅胶包，将讨论引向硅胶包外观与实际用途的混淆。

• peterarmstrong对硅胶包的巨大内部表面积表示惊讶，认为这种描述像科幻小说中的内容。
• xfp提到，食品中的类似包通常是氧气吸收剂而非干燥剂，且这些氧气吸收剂不可重复使用，与硅胶包不同。

• amelius关心如何去除空气中的氧气以保持食物新鲜，询问是否有其他简单方法。
• eande介绍了超级吸水聚合物（SAP）的广泛应用，如尿布和植物水保留。

• zzbn00分享了个人经验，将硅胶包与打开的超级胶水瓶一起存放在冰箱中，延长胶水保存时间。

• 不同类型的干燥剂和吸湿材料（如氧气吸收剂和分子筛）在讨论中被比较，强调了它们的不同用途和局限性。
• 对硅胶包的误解和误用案例也被提及，增加了对正确使用方法的认识。
• 争议焦点在于硅胶包的实际效果和公众对其功能的误解。

How Silica Gel Took Over the World
Spencer Wright
I find them stuffed into the toes of a new pair of sneakers. I find them wedged into a sheaf of seaweed snacks. I find them in the over-inflated bag that contains my new inhaler, and in the vacuum-sealed one puckered around my kids’ 3D printing filament. “DO NOT EAT,” they all admonish me, and I find myself slipping them under the top layer of the garbage already in the trash can, as if my kids wouldn’t be able to control their urge to taste whatever is inside these tiny white pouches. Silica gel packets are
everywhere
, their presence seemingly the only thing keeping our packaged food crispy and our belongings free of mildew. How on earth did they all get here?
Is silica gel taking over the world?
Tear its little Tyvek wrapping, and spill a packet of glassy silica gel beads into the palm of your hand; they won’t hurt you. They are made of the same stuff as sand: “Silica” means “silicon dioxide,” which is the primary component of most drinkware, windshields, and the screen of whatever electronic device you’re reading this on. But glass has a density of around 2500 kilograms per cubic meter, and crystalline silicon dioxide (quartz) is around 2650. Silica gel, on the other hand, is more like 700 kilograms per cubic meter. It may look fully dense, but in fact it’s shot through with countless tiny pores. If your windowpane is like a thin sheet of solid ice, then a silica gel bead is like a tiny snowball.
Silica gel beads, as seen by a scanning electron microscope. Image credit: Dusan Berek, via
Structural inhomogeneities in wide-pore silica gels
.
Zoom in on a silica gel bead with a scanning electron microscope, and its smooth surface turns discontinuous, riddled with voids about 2.5 nanometers across (roughly the diameter of a strand of DNA). This microstructure gives silica gel radical properties. The silica gel packets in my kids’ seaweed snacks are just a little bit bigger than postage stamps, and have a total mass of about a gram. That single gram of silica gel could have an internal surface area of eight hundred square meters—the size of
almost two basketball courts
.
These factors allow silica gel to adsorb up to 40% of its own weight in water vapor, through a process called
capillary condensation
. When humid air migrates into the pores of a silica gel bead, its vapor pressure increases, causing water to condense onto the silica gel’s internal surfaces. At the risk of anthropomorphizing water, it’s as if it prefers to be a liquid, stuck within the silica gel’s tiny capillaries, than a vapor, carried along with whatever else is in the air.
At the risk of anthropomorphizing
myself
, I prefer writing engaging, evergreen essays like this one. I can only do so with the financial backing of readers like you.
Infrastructure is worth writing about
If you find a packet of silica gel in an imported snack or the pocket of a new jacket, it’s probably there to filter water vapor out of air. Like most filters, there is a limit to how much water a piece of silica gel can hold; its internal surfaces are finite in size, and as a result there is a finite amount of humidity that a given packet of silica gel can adsorb. Luckily, silica gel vendors offer nifty calculators so that their customers can size their silica gel packets to the volumes of air they wish to dry out—and how dry they want the air to be. If you wanted to desiccate the air inside of a child’s balloon, you’d calculate its volume (let’s call it 14 liters), then make some assumptions about its temperature and humidity (around 35°C, 75% RH), then decide what you want its final relative humidity to be (let’s bring it down to 20% RH). Run these numbers and you’d find you needed to pull about 0.3 grams of water out of the air in your balloon. This can be done, pretty reliably, with a one- or two-gram packet of silica gel, slipped into the balloon just before you blow it up.

Of course, different applications will entail different goals. The bag that holds your potato chips is not
completely
impermeable to moisture, and if you’re going to ship it across an ocean and then let it sit on a shelf for a few months, you should expect some additional water vapor to find its way in. There are also applications in which silica gel is used not so much to dry something out but to maintain a particular equilibrium humidity. In the art world, silica gel packets are slipped into exhibit cases and
used for their “buffering capacity,”
helping maintain a stable (and relatively high) humidity inside the case while conditions in the rest of the gallery might vary.

data.title: How AI is creating a rift at McKinsey, Bain, and BCG
data.author: rustoo
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了AI工具在咨询公司中的应用及其影响。随着客户对AI工具的接触增加，麦肯锡、BCG和贝恩等顶级咨询公司正转向基于实施的模式，并将AI广泛应用于项目中。初级顾问被鼓励使用AI进行研究、策略制定和创意构思，但因时间大幅缩短感到不满。公司高层如经理和合伙人看好AI，认为它能提高效率，但基层顾问认为AI压缩了他们的创造性和工作质量。尽管AI缩小了公司与客户间的知识差距，但过度依赖AI导致不切实际的工作预期和质量下降，初级顾问承担了大部分压力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对管理咨询行业的影响以及潜在的变革

不同观点：
• **AI对管理咨询影响有限，仅增强现有模式**：tharne认为，管理咨询的核心是作为高管的“保险”，AI只是帮助生成报告、图表等，不会改变行业本质。CEO可以利用AI生成的材料将成功归功于自己，将失败归咎于外部因素或经济环境。
• **AI使咨询工作更加冗余**：mawadev和WorkerBee28474指出，AI让管理咨询师显得更加多余，因为AI可以完成许多咨询任务，尤其是低级别的数据处理和报告生成工作。
• **AI对咨询行业的未来产生深远影响**：alabastervlog提到，未来咨询报告的制作将越来越多地依赖AI工具，甚至已经部分外包给印度等国家。newfocogi分享了McKinsey内部对AI替代软件开发人员的讨论，表明AI对高技能岗位也有潜在威胁。
• **AI可能替代初级岗位，但高级岗位仍安全**：alephnerd承认AI对初级岗位（如助理和初级顾问）构成威胁，但认为高端管理咨询等“核心职能”仍然难以被替代。
• **AI将广泛替代高薪职业**：game_the0ry认为，如果AI能替代软件工程师，那么其他高薪职业（如法律、医疗等）也将受到冲击，尤其是那些高劳动力成本的行业。
• **AI压缩开发者工作时间并减少创造力**：Seattle3503从开发者的角度指出，AI虽然提升了效率，但也导致项目时间被压缩，创造力受到影响。

补充讨论：
• **咨询公司的透明度问题**：gessha提问，上市公司是否披露雇佣咨询公司（如McKinsey）的情况。
• **AI替代大部分咨询师的可行性**：SpaceManNabs质疑，如果咨询师的工作可以外包或由AI完成，那么咨询公司为何不直接用AI替代大部分员工。
• **AI在公共项目中的潜在滥用**：justlikereddit批评了AI可能替代咨询人员在公共项目中的角色，认为这可能导致更糟糕的项目实施，而利润却被少数人获取。

争议焦点：
• **AI是否会彻底改变管理咨询行业**：一方认为AI只是增强现有咨询模式，另一方认为AI将替代大量咨询师，尤其是初级岗位，并对行业产生深远影响。

43549099.article_content:
Read Summary
Clients’ increasing access to AI tools is transforming the way consulting firms operate
Apart from moving towards an implementation-based model, the Big 3—McKinsey, BCG and Bain—are now incorporating AI in a major chunk of their projects
Consultants at the juniormost level are encouraged to use AI for research, strategy and ideation. Albeit on considerably shortened timelines
Thoughts on AI vary across the firms’ hierarchy—while managers and partners love it, consultants who are closer to the ground view things differently
Enter your email address to receive a daily summary of all our stories.
“Why are you solving this problem from first principles? You should’ve used ChatGPT to help you.”
A consultant at Boston Consulting Group (BCG), one of the “Big 3s” in the sector, recounted their manager’s reaction when they turned in a preliminary report on a certain topic a few months ago. “The funniest part is that I
had
used ChatGPT to solve the problem. I just hadn’t told my manager,” they said, not wanting to be named as they weren’t authorised to speak with the media.
Welcome to management consulting in 2025, where much of what you see on a consultant’s deck has been outsourced to generative AI tools—including, funnily enough, the deck itself. You’d think firms would be wary of this new technology that threatens to make them obsolete. After all, AI has considerably
narrowed
Innolead
The End of Consulting as We Know it: Client Power and the AI Revolution
the knowledge gap between firms and clients, as one McKinsey consultant admitted. Instead, firms are enthusiastically adopting AI across the board.
Those on the “frontlines” of the industry’s AI pivot are the consultants—the junior-most employees at firms like BCG tasked with research and number crunching. And it seems like they’re not happy about it. Instead of making their life easier, AI has resulted in drastically reduced timelines and ebbing appreciation for creativity.
“A lot of senior partners and partners think of AI as a magic bullet,” said a former manager at Bain, another of the Big 3 consultancies. For instance, a senior partner who assigned his juniors to work on a
client assessment
client assessment
a systematic process of gathering and analysing information about a client's business, goals, and challenges to determine the best course of action
thought they could use an AI chatbot to parse data and ready the assessment in a day, said the former manager. The same thing would have earlier taken two to three weeks.
But here’s the thing: even with AI, a day is an unrealistic deadline for an assignment like this. So, who bears the brunt of these outsized expectations? The runt of the litter: the consultants. When rushed, they end up turning in subpar, AI-generated copy that sounds nice but doesn’t mean much.

data.title: In Defence of TypeScript Enums
data.author: romellem
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TypeScript中enum实现的优缺点

不同观点：
• [TheCycoONE] 认为，批评的重点不是enum的概念本身，而是TypeScript中enum的实现。他指出，TypeScript的enum编译成JavaScript对象时会产生泄漏的抽象，导致许多潜在问题（footguns）。他还提到TypeScript在某些设计决策上似乎是为了可擦除性，比如导入文件使用js扩展名而不是ts扩展名。一个好的语言特性应该自然融入开发过程。

• [miningape] 同意对TypeScript enums的批评，认为它们表面上与其它语言的enum相似，给人一种熟悉和舒适的错觉，但在实际使用中由于需要在TypeScript和JavaScript之间进行桥接，导致抽象泄漏。他建议使用纯JavaScript对象或TypeScript的字面量联合类型作为替代方案。

• [tengbretson] 反驳了反对使用字面量联合类型的声音，指出在使用字面量联合类型时，像`if (color === "Red")`这样的代码会导致编译错误ts(2367)，从而进一步论证了使用字面量联合类型的好处。

• [koshdim] 对文章表示赞赏，认为文章清晰地定义了TypeScript中enum的范围和用途。虽然由于一些限制，他在使用enum的频率上比在C#中少，但仍然认为enum在合适的场景中是有用的。

补充讨论：
• [paulddraper] 引用了GitHub上的一个未解决的TypeScript问题[1]，指出虽然文章努力为enum辩护，但无法使用symbol类型的事实使得这种辩护变得无力。

[1] https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/18408

data.title: New in Gmail: Making E2E encrypted emails easy to use for all organizations
data.author: skim
data.article_summary: Google宣布在Gmail中引入简化的端到端加密电子邮件功能，使各类组织能够轻松发送加密邮件。以往，端到端加密邮件由于S/MIME的复杂性和专有解决方案的高成本，仅限于拥有大量IT资源的大型组织。Google通过新的解决方案，让企业用户只需几次点击即可向任何邮箱发送加密邮件，无需交换证书或使用自定义软件。对于非Gmail用户，Google会发送邀请，使其通过受限版Gmail查看和回复加密邮件。IT团队无需再处理复杂的证书管理，同时还能控制数据访问和安全性。该功能通过客户端加密（CSE）实现，确保加密密钥由客户自行控制，增强数据隐私和安全。这项新功能现已进入测试阶段，并将逐步推广。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google客户端加密功能及其相关的用户体验和隐私问题

不同观点：
• [对功能真实性的质疑]
  ◦ [ninjastar99] 认为该功能看起来像愚人节的玩笑，尤其是UI设计和要求用户登录的行为，像极了钓鱼邮件。
  ◦ [CyanLite2] 直接称该功能为愚人节玩笑。
  
• [对隐私和安全性的担忧]
  ◦ [cachedthing0] 将Google与隐私问题联系起来，暗示Google在隐私方面的声誉不佳，并再次提到愚人节，质疑功能的真实性或实用性。
  ◦ [egberts] 对在JavaScript网站上实现端到端加密（E2EE）表示强烈不信任，认为这种方式不安全。

• [对用户体验和诈骗风险的关注]
  ◦ [d332] 认为该功能的用户体验设计可能成为诈骗者的便利工具，尤其是从演示视频来看。
  
• [对功能机制的疑问]
  ◦ [rlpb] 关心当收件人是Gmail用户时，加密邮件如何在收件箱中自动解密，并询问对搜索功能的影响。
  
• [对功能推出的看法]
  ◦ [blitzar] 质疑该功能是否原本是为政府机构设计的，只是顺便让普通企业使用。
  ◦ [commandersaki] 提到这是Google第三次或第四次尝试推出加密邮件功能，暗示对Google之前尝试的不满或怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 用户对Google在隐私和安全性方面的信任问题是一个重要的讨论点，许多人对Google的加密功能持怀疑态度。
• 用户体验设计（如登录要求和UI外观）被认为是潜在的安全风险，容易被诈骗者利用。
• 功能的技术实现（如JavaScript上的E2E加密）和自动解密机制引发了对安全性及其实际操作的进一步质疑。

争议焦点：
• Google客户端加密功能的实际安全性和隐私保护能力。
• 用户体验设计是否增加了钓鱼风险。
• 该功能是否值得信任以及Google在加密邮件方面的多次尝试为何未能获得用户信任。

43547863.article_content:
Identity and Security
New in Gmail:
Making end-to-end encrypted emails easy to use for all organizations
April 1, 2025
Johney Burke
Senior Product Manager, Google Workspace
Julien Duplant
Product Manager, Google Workspace
Try Google Workspace at No Cost
Get a business email, all the storage you need, video conferencing, and more.
SIGN UP
At Google, we believe that secure, confidential communication should be available for organizations of all sizes. However, end-to-end encrypted (E2EE) email was historically a privilege reserved for organizations with significant IT resources, due to the complexity of S/MIME and proprietary solutions. Over the past two years, we've made
progress
in breaking down these barriers, simplifying E2EE, to help customers address their critical compliance and data sovereignty needs. But we knew there was more work to do to truly democratize it.
Today is Gmail’s
birthday
, and we wanted to do something special —
enable enterprise users to send E2EE messages to any user on any email inbox with just a few clicks
.
This capability, requiring minimal efforts for both IT teams and end users, abstracts away the traditional IT complexity and substandard user experiences of existing solutions, while preserving enhanced data sovereignty, privacy, and security controls. We’re rolling this out in a phased approach, starting today, in beta, with the ability to send E2EE emails to Gmail users in your own organization. In the coming weeks, users will be able to send E2EE emails to any Gmail inbox, and, later this year, to any email inbox. Let’s take a closer look.
Sending an E2EE email to a non-Gmail user
The current state of encrypted email — the good, the bad, and the unpleasant
Most enterprise email providers encrypt customer data at rest and in transit. Gmail does it
by default
. The Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) is a protocol that enables sending digitally signed and encrypted messages. It is typically used for highly-sensitive emails among regulated organizations, such as government agencies and businesses that work with them.
While more organizations have real needs for E2EE emails, few have the resources to implement S/MIME. IT teams need to acquire and manage certificates and deploy them to each user, resulting in additional efforts and costs. And end users have to figure out whether they and the recipient have S/MIME configured (few do), and then go through the hassle of exchanging certificates before the encrypted emails can be exchanged. This often results in frustration and the inability to send encrypted emails.
Alternatives to S/MIME, such as encryption features from email providers or proprietary point solutions, present significant drawbacks as well: the former requires sharing encryption keys, increasing data privacy and sovereignty risks, while the latter complicates end user experiences with custom applications, portals, or browser extensions. We think there should be a simpler and more efficient way.
Sending end-to-end encrypted emails to any inbox with Gmail
The idea here is simple. Email messages are encrypted with just a few clicks in Gmail regardless of who they are being sent to — no need for end users to exchange certificates or use custom software. The emails are protected using encryption keys controlled by the customer and not available to Google servers, providing enhanced data privacy and security. And the IT team no longer needs to go through the complex S/MIME setup or certificate management. This is how it works behind the scenes:
When the recipient is a Gmail user (enterprise or personal), Gmail sends an E2EE email. The email is automatically decrypted in the recipient's inbox, and the recipient can use Gmail in a familiar way.
When the recipient is not a Gmail user, Gmail sends them an invitation to view the E2EE email in a restricted version of Gmail. The recipient can then use a guest Google Workspace account to securely view and reply to the email.
When the recipient has S/MIME configured, Gmail sends an E2EE email via S/MIME (just like it does today).
Securely viewing an E2EE email in a restricted version of Gmail
IT teams also have the option to require all external recipients (even if they are Gmail users) to use the restricted version of Gmail. This helps ensure that their organization’s data does not end up stored on third-party servers and devices. It also makes it easier for organizations to protect their data by having the ability to apply security policies and revoke access to emails, no matter how long ago they were sent. Essentially, the E2EE email becomes like a document in Google Drive, allowing the IT team to control its access.
This new capability is powered by
client-side encryption
(CSE), a technical control in Workspace, that helps organizations to protect their sensitive emails, documents, calendar events, and meetings using encryption keys that are under their sole control and stored outside of Google’s infrastruct

data.title: Swift Achieved Dynamic Linking Where Rust Couldn't
data.author: misterdata
data.article_summary: 本文主要探讨了Swift如何实现ABI稳定性和动态链接，而Rust未能做到这一点。Swift 5实现了ABI稳定性，这是其重要特性之一，使得Swift能够在不影响语言设计的前提下实现动态链接。ABI稳定性允许系统API在不同版本间保持兼容，从而实现动态链接，使得应用程序无需重新编译即可使用新版系统库。这篇文章简要比较了Swift和Rust的设计，指出Swift通过精心设计的类型布局、调用约定和符号名称，确保了ABI的稳定性，从而实现动态链接。Swift的ABI策略包括对类型布局的严格定义、函数调用的标准化以及符号的统一管理，确保不同模块间的兼容性。文章还提到，动态链接对操作系统尤为重要，因为它允许系统库的更新不影响使用这些库的应用程序，并减少内存占用。Swift通过这些机制实现了更高层次的ABI稳定性，而Rust则因为设计上的不同选择，尚未实现类似的动态链接功能。
