data.title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (March 2025)
data.author: david927
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多个技术项目的进展和实现细节

不同观点：
• **[enisberk]** 认为在低资源音频分类中，标注数据是瓶颈，因此其研究聚焦于通过主动学习、迁移学习、数据估值和跨模态学习等方式，在少数据情况下获得良好结果。他创建了EDANSA数据集并改进了主动学习方法。
• **[taejavu]** 开发了一个简易的发票生成器，解决了移动端生成发票时现有工具界面笨重、强制注册等问题。他通过将状态存储在URL中，实现了便捷的发票共享和访问。
• **[andrethegiant]** 创建了pure.md工具，允许用户将网页转换为Markdown格式，避免了机器人检测，并能处理JavaScript较重的网站。他认为这可以作为LLM的全局缓存层。
• **[megadragon9]** 开发了一个类似于PyTorch API的机器学习库，完全从零使用Python和NumPy构建，旨在帮助初学者理解模型学习的底层机制。
• **[999900000999]** 创建了一个受万智牌启发的开源数字卡牌游戏，反对当前数字卡牌游戏的商业模式，希望通过开源方式让玩家有更多自由。
• **[maxwelljoslyn]** 致力于将传统RPG与计算机融合，批评当前虚拟桌面应用（VTTs）的局限性，并开发了一个实验性的应用来实现其理想的功能。

补充讨论：
• **[amrangaye]** 开发了一个基于GPT接口的“氛围编码”工具，可以将自己的女儿插入非洲童话故事中，并计划将这些故事在线发布，以推广非洲历史。
• **[greysteil]** 创建了mentions.us，用于监控关键词在多个平台上的提及情况，解决了Reddit等大规模数据源的技术挑战，但目前用户主要在免费 tier。
• **[mhuffman]** 更新了一个名为"Date Night Movie Player"的应用，用于远程情侣同步观看视频并聊天，具有一些有趣的功能如“啤酒休息”按钮。
• **[icy]** 开发了基于Bluesky’s AT Protocol的协作平台Tangled，旨在重新思考和改进GitHub的功能，例如堆叠PRs等。
• **[hedayet]** 创建了一个无AI、仅限人类社交的网络平台，强调隐私保护和与亲密联系人的简单互动，反对主流社交媒体的算法操控。
• **[kamranjon]** 经营一家小型公司，设计和3D打印16mm电影摄影机配件，同时在在线教育公司工作，研究知识追踪和学习路径。
• **[janosch_123]** 分享了其在电动汽车领域的经验，通过多个平台传播知识，并利用之前在转换伦敦出租车项目中的经验。
• **[itwenty]** 开发了iOS应用MergeFit，用于合并Apple Watch上的运动记录，解决了运动记录中断的问题，并实现了无互联网情况下操作。
• **[Saigonautica]** 开发了多个硬件项目，包括个人图书馆管理应用、量子RNG设备、E2E加密聊天设备等，强调了硬件迭代的缓慢和其持续创造的动力。

争议焦点：
• **低资源数据处理**：[enisberk]的研究和[megadragon9]对底层机制的理解在解决数据瓶颈问题上有不同的技术路径和侧重点。
• **数字卡牌游戏商业模式**：[999900000999]对现有数字卡牌游戏的商业模式持批评态度，并提出开源替代方案。
• **虚拟桌面应用的功能**：[maxwelljoslyn]对当前VTTs的功能不满意，提出了更具灵活性和创造性的解决方案。

这些讨论展示了不同开发者在技术实现、商业模式和用户需求上的多样化视角和实践经验。

data.title: Ask HN: Who is hiring? (April 2025)
data.author: whoishiring
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同公司和岗位在招聘软件工程师、AI工程师及相关技术职位的条件、要求和公司文化。

不同观点：
• **Omi（kodjima33）**：Omi正在寻找创始工程师，公司发展迅速，已有30万用户和200万美元的融资。他们要求候选人有实际产品开发经验，使用的技术栈包括Flutter和C，并计划转向React Native。候选人需具备消费级硬件产品架构经验。

• **OpenAI（delqn）**：OpenAI的云基础设施团队正在招聘Kubernetes、Envoy和Istio方面的工程师。公司提供构建ChatGPT和OpenAI API基础平台的机会。

• **SerpApi（davidsojevic）**：SerpApi提供从初级到高级全栈工程师职位，支持远程工作，使用Ruby、Rails、MongoDB和React.JS技术栈。公司文化强调透明度、远程工作和利润分享。

• **Guilde（sbrown12）**：Guilde正在寻找高级工程师，专注于数据模型的开发。公司提供远程工作机会，要求候选人具备后端经验，并使用Golang、Postgres等技术。

• **Fathom（madiganf）**：Fathom正在招聘全栈工程师，公司提供AI Notetaker产品，正在快速增长。公司文化强调高效协作和快速出货。

• **Forward（amays_fwd）**：Forward正在寻找高级前端工程师，要求有NextJS和设计经验，开发嵌入式支付功能。公司提供现场和混合工作模式。

• **Clio（cliornd）**：Clio提供多个工程经理、机器学习工程师和DevOps工程师职位，要求在多伦多、卡尔加里或伯纳比以外的远程工作。公司提供永久全职职位和福利。

• **Navico（danicriss）**：Navico是一家海洋电子公司，要求候选人具备Android平台开发经验，能够处理从传感器数据读取到业务逻辑的开发。公司提供混合工作模式，要求在奥克兰本地。

• **Stellar Science（StellarScience）**：Stellar Science招聘科学软件开发工程师，要求候选人具备物理、工程、数学或计算机科学学位，使用C++、Qt等技术。公司提供实习和全职职位。

• **Sourcegraph（dcsourcegraph）**：Sourcegraph招聘多个工程师职位，公司使用AI加速软件开发，提供远程工作机会。公司强调高复杂度代码库的开发和维护。

• **Articulate（ggralla）**：Articulate招聘AI全栈工程师，公司提供AI Assistant产品，正在开发AI赋能的学习工具。公司要求候选人具备AI应用开发的热情，提供全远程工作机会。

• **Fleetio（Fleetio）**：Fleetio提供多个技术职位，包括AI工程师和软件工程师，公司提供SaaS平台，管理车辆和设备。公司提供全远程工作机会和丰厚福利。

• **FinQuery（roycoding）**：FinQuery招聘AI工程师，公司使用LLM和传统ML开发产品功能，提供远程工作机会。公司要求候选人具备2年以上工作经验。

• **Shortwave（mayop100）**：Shortwave正在快速增长，招聘AI代理工程师和产品工程师，公司提供商业通信产品，要求候选人在旧金山现场工作。

• **EliotNest（fahimf）**：EliotNest招聘创始工程师，公司使用AI/ML打击欺诈，要求候选人具备高度使命感和工作热情，提供纽约现场工作机会。

补充讨论：
• **工作模式**：多个公司提供远程工作机会，如SerpApi、Guilde、Fathom、Forward、Clio、Fleetio、FinQuery、Articulate。而Omi、Shortwave和EliotNest则要求现场或混合工作模式。

• **技术栈**：不同公司使用的技术栈各异，如Omi的Flutter和C，SerpApi的Ruby和Rails，Guilde的Golang和Postgres，Navico的Android和C/C++，Stellar Science的C++和Qt。

• **公司文化**：一些公司强调透明度（SerpApi）、远程工作（Fleetio、FinQuery）、使命感（EliotNest）、快速出货（Fathom、Shortwave）和高效协作（Clio、Fathom）。

争议焦点：
• **远程工作与现场工作**：一些公司提供全远程工作机会，而另一些公司则要求现场或混合工作模式，这在候选人选择职位时可能引发争议。

data.title: Move fast, break things: A review of Abundance by Ezra Klein and Derek Thompson
data.author: jaypinho
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《Abundance》一书及其相关住房政策的 various perspectives 和讨论

不同观点：
• **davidw**：认为书中的住房部分非常准确，住房短缺的影响是真实存在的，并且可以通过地方和州级别的努力来改善。他指出，住房不足导致通勤时间延长、CO2排放增加、与家人相处时间减少、城市扩张等问题。同时，他还提到“Abundance”概念较为模糊，但住房问题在美国是一个少见的跨党派议题。

• **owenpalmer**：通过自己父亲的建房经历说明，过度的法规（如县级的湿地规定和道路建设限制）是住房危机的重要原因之一。他特别提到，在华盛顿州，许多住房问题是由过度监管导致的。

• **velcrovan**：引用了一篇书评，将《Abundance》与Ezra Klein的医保讨论进行对比，暗示《Abundance》的议题可能面临与Klein类似的政策实施难题，因为这些建议需要对抗一些强大的利益集团。

• **tptacek**：批评某些评论对Ezra Klein的书进行了误解，指出Klein和Thompson提倡的策略是通过实际的建设来改善住房问题，而不是通过大规模的公共支出项目。他还提到YIMBY运动（支持增加住房的运动）和进步主义者之间的对立，认为某些对Klein的攻击是出于党派内部的动态。

• **Panzer04**：提出即使在“正和世界”中，改变也会有赢家和输家。住房政策的变化可能会让一些现有房主利益受损，补偿机制可能难以实施。他认为这个问题非常复杂，需要更多的思考和实验。

• **gcanyon**：认为书评可能没有抓住书的核心观点，即有些法规是需要保留的，有些是需要废除的。他强调，首先需要承认有些法规确实阻碍了进步，然后才能讨论如何改进。

• **pj_mukh**：批评一些评论过于简单化，希望找到一种“万用框架”来解决所有问题。他指出，快速高效的建设需要根据具体情况进行调整，而不是简单地归类为大政府或小政府的二元对立。

• **tgma**：引用《UNIX-HATERS Handbook》中的反讽内容，暗示Klein和Thompson在推销一种意识形态，试图通过批评现有体系来推动自己的议程。

• **xnx**：认为《Abundance》平台最重要的部分是它传达的积极信息，即通过认真重新评估现状，我们可以在长期存在的问题上取得进展。

• **rr808**：提到Lex Fridman的节目，暗示《Abundance》提倡的政策类似于供给侧经济学。

• **mkoubaa**：指出美国的政治文化以法律和诉讼为主，与中国的工程背景形成对比，认为这种文化很难通过一本书来改变。

• **wg0**：质疑关税政策是否能够推动“Abundance”和建设的革命。

• **ilrwbwrkhv**：批评像Peter Thiel和Marc Andreessen这样的人虽然能提出对社会的批评，但自己并没有创造出更美好的社会，指出他们的批评缺乏实际行动的支持。

补充讨论：
• **关于Marc Andreessen的争议**：多位评论者（如vvpan和tptacek）提到Andreessen反对自己所在城镇的多户住宅开发，与他之前发表的“Time to Build”文章中的观点相矛盾，显示出一种虚伪的立场。

• **党派和意识形态冲突**：tptacek和velcrovan提到了《Abundance》和Klein议题面临的党派冲突，特别是进步主义者与YIMBY运动之间的对立，反映出政策实施中存在的复杂政治动态。

data.title: Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models (Anthropic)
data.author: ydnyshhh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种揭示语言模型行为背后机制的方法——电路追踪（Circuit Tracing）。该方法通过使用一个更易解释的组件（跨层转码器，cross-layer transcoder）替代原模型中部分多层感知机（MLP）组件，构建一个“替代模型”来追踪计算步骤，生成计算图（attribution graphs）。研究团队开发了一系列可视化和验证工具，用于分析18层语言模型的简单行为，并为后续应用于更前沿模型（如Claude 3.5 Haiku）奠定基础。该方法旨在解决模型神经元的多义性（polysemantic）问题，通过稀疏编码模型（如转码器）分解模型激活，识别出可解释的特征，并研究这些特征如何交互形成电路。本文详细描述了方法论选择和跨层转码器的应用，以简化电路分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕深度学习模型的机制可解释性及其与遗传编程等技术的比较，讨论了模型的可解释性、训练数据的泛化能力、计算资源的消耗以及研究投入的问题。

不同观点：
• [bob1029] 认为深度学习模型的机制可解释性非常重要，尤其是通过遗传编程等技术可以实现模型的透明性。他指出，这种方式虽然计算量大，但借助现代硬件（如x86 CPU），可以快速搜索大量程序，从而实现高效的模型探索。他还提到，这种方法的缺点是搜索空间非常复杂，不能依赖数学技巧来简化计算，但整体上认为20世纪的一些想法在今天依然可行。

• [ironbound] 同意机制可解释性对于模型训练和对其行为的对齐（alignment）有重要作用，并建议通过一些视频资源帮助新手理解这一领域的技术细节。他特别提到了Anthropic公司在研究模型内部机制上的潜在收益。

• [xigency] 对当前一些研究者或机构在未深入理解模型内部机制的情况下获得大量研究资金表示不满，暗示这些研究者可能只是表面理解，并没有真正掌握模型的工作原理。

补充讨论：
• [somethingsome] 提出了一个实际问题，询问是否有相关的PDF资料可以获取，这表明讨论中可能需要更多书面资料来帮助理解。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于机制可解释性是否真的如[bob1029]所说可以带来显著的模型改进和数据效率提升，以及在实际应用中，研究者是否真正理解模型的内部机制，还是仅仅依赖于表面理解获得研究资金。这反映了理论可行性与实际应用之间的差距。

Transformer Circuits Thread
Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models
Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models
We introduce a method to uncover mechanisms underlying behaviors of language models. We produce graph descriptions of the model’s computation on prompts of interest by tracing individual computational steps in a “replacement model”. This replacement model substitutes a more interpretable component (here, a “cross-layer transcoder”) for parts of the underlying model (here, the multi-layer perceptrons) that it is trained to approximate. We develop a suite of visualization and validation tools we use to investigate these “attribution graphs” supporting simple behaviors of an 18-layer language model, and lay the groundwork for a
companion paper
applying these methods to a frontier model, Claude 3.5 Haiku.

Author contributions statement below
.
Introduction
Deep learning models produce their outputs using a series of transformations distributed across many computational units (artificial “neurons”). The field of
mechanistic interpretability
seeks to describe these transformations in human-understandable language. To date, our team’s approach has followed a two-step approach. First, we identify
features
, interpretable building blocks that the model uses in its computations. Second, we describe the processes, or
circuits,
by which these features interact to produce model outputs.
A natural approach is to use the raw neurons of the model as these building blocks.
An alternative approach is to study the roles of gross model components such as entire MLP blocks and attention heads
. This approach has identified interesting roles these components play in specific behaviors, but large components play a multitude of unrelated roles across the data distribution, so we seek a more granular decomposition.
Using this approach, previous work successfully identified interesting circuits in vision models, built out of neurons that appear to represent meaningful visual concepts
. However, model neurons are often
polysemantic
— representing a mixture of many unrelated concepts. One reason for polysemanticity is thought to be the phenomenon of
superposition
, in which models must represent more concepts than they have neurons, and thus must “smear” their representation of concepts across many neurons. This mismatch between the network's basic computational units (neurons) and meaningful concepts has proved a major impediment to progress to the mechanistic agenda, especially in understanding language models.
In recent years, sparse coding models such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs)
, transcoders
, and crosscoders
have emerged as promising tools for identifying interpretable features represented in superposition. These methods decompose model activations into sparsely active components (“features”),
We use 'feature' following the tradition of 'feature detectors' in neuroscience and 'feature learning' in machine learning. Some recent literature uses the term 'latent,' which refers to specific vectors in the model's latent space. We find 'feature' better captures the computational role these elements play, making it more appropriate for describing transcoder neurons than SAE decoder vectors.
which turn out in many cases to correspond to human-interpretable concepts. While current sparse coding methods are an imperfect way of identifying features (see
§ Limitations
), they produce interpretable enough results that we are motivated to study
circuits
composed of these features. Several authors have already made promising steps in this direction
.
Although the basic premise of studying circuits built out of sparse coding features sounds simple, the design space is large. In this paper we describe our current approach, which involves several key methodological decisions:
Transcoders.
We extract features using a variant of
transcoders
rather than SAEs, which allows us to construct an interpretable “replacement model” that can be studied as a proxy for the original model. Importantly, this approach allows us to analyze direct feature-feature interactions.
Cross-Layer.
We base our analysis on cross-layer transcoders (CLT)
, in which each feature reads from the residual stream at one layer and contributes to the outputs of all subsequent MLP layers of the original model, which greatly simplifies the resulting

data.title: Stop syncing everything
data.author: neilk
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了Graft，一个由Carl Sverre推出的开源事务存储引擎，专为实现懒惰和部分复制而设计，具有强一致性、水平可扩展性和对象存储的持久性。Graft解决了在边缘设备和离线环境中有效同步数据的问题，避免了全量复制的高开销和逻辑复制的复杂性。其核心是通过“卷”（Volume）和“页”（Pages）实现数据的部分同步，客户端可以根据需要选择同步内容和时间，从而实现高效的部分复制。Graft适用于离线优先、跨平台同步、无状态多写入副本等场景，支持任意数据类型的复制，并提供强一致性保证。文章还介绍了Graft的“懒惰”特性，允许客户端自行决定同步节奏，以及通过元数据实现精准的部分同步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Graft系统的设计和一致性模型，尤其是其提交和冲突处理机制，以及与其他类似系统的比较。

不同观点：
• [kiitos] 对Graft的"本地提交"和"异步远程提交"机制感到困惑，认为这种模型混淆了多种"提交"概念，并质疑如何处理异步提交失败后的回滚问题。

Stop syncing everything
Carl Sverre
March 2025
Partial replication sounds easy—just sync the data your app needs, right? But choosing an approach is tricky: logical replication precisely tracks every change, complicating strong consistency, while physical replication avoids that complexity but requires syncing every change, even discarded ones.
What if your app could combine the simplicity of physical replication with the efficiency of logical replication?
That’s the key idea behind
Graft
, the open-source transactional storage engine I’m launching today. It’s designed specifically for lazy, partial replication with strong consistency, horizontal scalability, and object storage durability.
Graft is designed with the following
use cases
in mind:
Offline-first & mobile apps
:
Simplify development
and improve reliability by offloading replication and storage to Graft.
Cross-platform sync
: Share data smoothly across devices, browsers, and platforms without vendor lock-in.
Stateless multi-writer replicas
: Deploy replicas anywhere, including serverless and embedded environments.
Any data type
: Replicate databases, files, or custom formats—all with strong consistency.
I first discovered the need for Graft while building
SQLSync
. SQLSync is a frontend optimized database stack built on top of
SQLite
with a synchronization engine powered by ideas from Git and distributed systems. SQLSync makes multiplayer SQLite databases a reality, powering interactive apps that run directly in your browser.
However, SQLSync replicates the entire log of changes to every client—similar to how some databases implement physical replication. While this approach works fine on servers, it’s poorly suited to the constraints of edge and browser environments.
After shipping SQLSync, I decided to find a replication solution more suited to the edge. I needed something that could:
Let clients
sync at their own pace
Sync only what they need
Sync from anywhere
, including the edge and offline devices
Replicate
arbitrary data
1
All while providing
strong consistency guarantees
.
That didn’t exist. So I built it.
#
A different approach to edge replication
If you’ve ever tried to keep data in sync across clients and servers, you know it’s harder than it sounds. Most existing solutions fall into one of two camps:
Full replication
, which syncs the entire dataset to each client—not practical for constrained environments like serverless functions or web apps.
Schema-aware diffs
, like
Change Data Capture (CDC)
or
Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs)
, which track logical changes at the row or field level—but require deep application integration and don’t generalize to arbitrary data.
Graft takes a different path.
Like full replication, Graft is schema-agnostic. It doesn’t know or care what kind of data you’re storing—it just replicates bytes
2
. But instead of sending all the data, it behaves more like logical replication: clients receive a compact description of what’s changed since their last sync.
At the core of this model is the Volume: a sparse, ordered collection of fixed-size Pages. Clients interact with Volumes through a transactional API, reading and writing at specific Snapshots. Under the hood, Graft persists and replicates only what’s necessary—using object storage as a durable, scalable backend.
The result is a system that’s lazy, partial, edge-capable, and consistent.
Want to try the managed version of Graft?
Join the waitlist to get early access:
Sign up here →
Each of these properties deserves a closer look—let’s unpack them one by one.
#
Lazy: Sync at your own pace
Graft is designed for the real world—where edge clients wake up occasionally, face unreliable networks, and run in short-lived, resource-constrained environments. Instead of relying on continuous replication, clients choose
when
to sync, and Graft makes it easy to fast forward to the latest snapshot.
That sync starts with a simple question:
what changed since my last snapshot?
The server responds with a
graft
—a compact bitset of page indexes that have changed across all commits since that snapshot
3
. This is where the project gets its name: a
graft
attaches new changes to an existing snapshot—like grafting a branch onto a tree. They act as a guide, informing the
client which pages can be reused and which need to be fetched if needed.
Critically, when a client pulls a
graft
from the server, it doesn’t receive any actual data—only metadata about what changed. This gives the client full control over what to fetch and when, laying the foundation for partial replication.
#
Partial: Sync only what’s needed
When you’re building for edge environments—browser tabs, mobile apps, serverless functions—you can’t afford to download the entire dataset just to serve a handful of queries. That’s where partial replication comes in.
After a client pulls a
graft
, it knows exactly what’s changed. It can use that information to determine precisely which pages are still valid an

data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个使用Raspberry Pi和电子墨水屏（E-Ink）构建的火车与天气追踪器项目。该设备能显示纽约地铁F线和G线的到站时间以及通勤天气，帮助作者和妻子更轻松地掌握出行时间，而无需每次查看手机。设备采用9.7英寸电子墨水屏，通过MTA API获取实时火车信息，并显示当前时间和未来12小时的天气。软件部分采用了模块化设计，包括显示引擎、布局系统、数据服务和应用控制器。由于电子墨水屏的刷新率限制，项目采用混合更新策略以避免显示模糊和重影问题。该项目不仅实用，还深受作者妻子喜爱，代码和制作说明已在GitHub上分享。

43517439.article_content:
Train & Weather Tracker with Raspberry Pi & E-Ink
March 2, 2025
Art
,
Physical
,
Software
I finally built a Raspberry Pi project my wife loves: an e-ink train and weather tracker! If you want to build one yourself,
the Github & instructions are here.
Kira will be jogging to the night shift!
Over the past few years, I've been on something of an e-ink journey.  I started with a
weather and news display
(still the only post on my website that regularly gets organic traffic.) While I loved it and it looked great, a phone is a better way to check the news, and the weather only gets checked once a day. Then in 2022 while at MIT I built
Jarvis, the e-ink voice-to-image display
. Jarvis was a great party trick — say, "Hey Jarvis, paint me an elephant on a bowling ball in Times Square" and watch as the image gradually appeared. Notably, this was before ChatGPT, when people were still impressed by AI!
Jarvis live demo is better!
Then over Thanksgiving, I had some free time, a basket of spare parts, and the itch to code and build something physical. So here we are with the e-ink train and weather tracker.
The idea is simple: Every morning, my wife and I take the inbound F or G subway lines to work from a stop that's a 2-minute jog or a 6-minute walk from our house. I love the NYC subway and it works incredibly well, but the trains come
often
and
predictably
, not
on-a-schedule
. So every morning we're calling out, when's the next G, when's the next F — and one of us pulls out a phone for the MTA app or Google Maps and yells back the upcoming train times. Then we time our morning routines to either stretch for a train in three minutes or slow down for a train in ten.
The subway and weather tracker makes checking train times much faster and calmer than pulling out a phone. Since it's centrally located in our home, someone is always close enough to glance at it.
The subway times reported by the
MTA API
are reliable once the train is within a few stops or 15 minutes away, with precision increasing as the trains get closer. Having the train times on the wall lets you check how your morning routine is developing against the train schedule as the departure time gets closer.
Best of all, Kira loves it! This goes on my DIY pantheon along with adding legs to her dresser to make it a better height and fixing a towel rack right before she hosted her colleagues for a book club.
If you want to build one yourself or better understand the project, I'll dive into some editorial and gotchas below. The practical instructions, parts, and code live in this
GitHub Repo
.
Description & Features
The train & weather tracker is built on a
9.7" 1200x825 E-Ink display
attached to a
Raspberry Pi 4b
. The display is split into four parts: a header, with date, time, and a live second hand to indicate liveness; a train tracker; the commute weather; and a "weather bar" displaying the next 12 hours of weather. The main focus of the layout is the train tracker, which shows the upcoming 30 minutes of inbound F & G trains.
The display sits in a laser cut mat board with black ridges sized to hide the black border of the e-ink display. The mat board sits in a 8.5" x 11" cherry frame that is 1.5" deep to allow the raspberry pi to be backmounted while the frame is still flush to the wall. We hang the display next to the door above a key holder, which is generally the right place for it, but also helps hide the power cord.
Not pretty, but it works
Project Details
The software portion of the project is manageable although there are some gotchas when programming against the Waveshare e-ink hat in particular. We have a modular architecture with a clear separation of concerns:
Display Engine: Renders the layout to the display, supporting communication with the physical e-ink display or rendering a png for non-raspberry pi development
Layout System: A pretty hacky visual arrangement of the elements. It'd be fun to do something more sophisticated here (e.g. a html renderer), but 🤷‍♂️. This will likely require the most work if you want to modify the project
Data Services: Fetch & process (this is important!) train arrival from NYC Transit GTFS feeds + get the weather forecasts
Application Controller: Orchestrate the event loop and subscription model to drive updates to the display
The biggest technical constraint is the update rate to the e-ink display. The display supports multiple update modes with different tradeoffs and
can
manage sub 500 ms updates, especially for partial updates, but a faster refresh results in fuzzy characters and substantial ghosting that looks pretty bad. The bigger issue is that overloading the display causes it to crash, which requires a full reset.
After some testing, I chose a hybrid display update strategy.
Every second, the pixels around the seconds & minutes digits of the time are rerendered with the display's fastest partial update mode to make it clear that the display is functioning as expected.

Happy April Fool’s, but frankly we are all (well almost all) business today with a neat little update.
Kevin Hawickhorst’s article talked about Eisenhower-era process improvement tools that transformed federal efficiency during the 1940s-1960s, when government trust reached 80% and major national projects succeeded
. You know what? Why keep such a gem hidden away in old dusty books and digital pdf scans? We should create a documentation site with the intent of fully recreating, updating, and creating alternative versions of the Work Simplification program and the artifacts (training materials, art, etc)—not just for governments but for civic organizations, political campaigns, and businesses. The idea is to make it easier for today's organizations (or at least the common political actor local government employee) identify unnecessary procedural steps and eliminate bottlenecks that waste resources, maybe even spot loopholes and poison pills in bills and plans to spot for.
Right now we converted the associated manuals into a docs site called Standards, with our end of April plans is recreate the other materials like Process Chart forms and the such
Standards - Fork of Work Simplification
On that note, thanks for reading Governance Cybernetics! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support our work.
Subscribe
Why Does This Matter?
Process improvement isn't intuitive for most people. As stated in earlier articles, even big boy corporations with dedicated resources often struggle to implement it effectively (
don’t believe me, ask McKinsey who is less trustworthy than I am but for some reason, you trust these guys
). And while think tanks occasionally tackle implementation issues, they're typically far removed from the ground-level reality where policies succeed or fail.
We need to make process improvement accessible to ordinary people in local groups who have the most direct experience with broken processes. They don't need MBA jargon or complex methodologies—just practical tools to document what's happening in their communities. Practical tools like what the Work Simplification Program has to offer.
A hypothetical example is a local YIMBY volunteer who's helped ten homeowners navigate ADU permits and has invaluable knowledge that no policy expert in Sacramento possesses (which is a good idea in its own right, instead of an accounting student helping people file taxes, law or real estate students helping people navigate ADU permits with the understanding they are not real estate lawyers). Adjusting Work Simplification’s Process Charting (making a list of all the steps one by one and making them like a more verbose flowchart), so that volunteer with basic process mapping skills increases the chances that the volunteer might spot something everyone else overlooks!
Unlike corporate “process improvement” which focuses on short-term cost-cutting
or
(in very rare cases since Deming’s death) efficiency
, the WW2-era political process improvement focuses on effectiveness—making the government deliver what laws promise just like what happened during the 40s and 50s. This distinction matters because it centers on citizen experience rather than administrative convenience.
Even something as esoteric as increasing fertility rates,
there is a growing mountain of research and case studies showcasing the value of better implementation or even better local government can provide
, let’s say “booming” results (*sounds of crickets chirping* yes I want to make that joke again).
Recreating Work Simplification will help us deal with failures aren't about policy intent but process implementation.
On That Note
The consolidated training manual is called “Work Simplification as Exemplified by the Work Simplification Program of the U. S. Bureau of the Budget.” It is
online
on Hathitrust. To read it, you have to be located in the US. To download it, you have to have an institutional subscription. Or, you can reach out to me and I be glad to give you a digital pdf.

data.article_summary: SSLyze是一款快速强大的SSL/TLS扫描工具和Python库，用于分析服务器SSL/TLS配置，确保使用强加密并防范已知TLS攻击。它具有高速度和可靠性，支持扫描非HTTP服务器，如SMTP、LDAP等，并可通过Python API集成到应用中。扫描结果可保存为JSON文件，并能直接在CI/CD中使用以持续检查服务器合规性。SSLyze可通过pip或Docker安装，并提供详细的API文档和使用示例。该工具在AGPL-3.0许可证下发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：比较 **testssl.sh** 和 **sslyze** 两种 SSL/TLS 测试工具的优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持 testssl.sh**：[peblos] 更倾向于使用 **testssl.sh**，认为它的输出更具可读性，组织良好。同时指出 **sslyze** 在处理 TLS 版本检查（如 TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3）和 Mozilla TLS 配置合规性检查时出现了错误信息（tracebacks），影响使用体验。
  
• **潜在的 sslyze 优势**：虽然 [peblos] 更偏好 testssl.sh，但他也表示愿意了解 **sslyze** 是否有其他显著的优势。这表明 sslyze 可能在某些场景或功能上有其独特之处，但尚未明确指出。

补充讨论：
• **工具的完整性**：[peblos] 认为 **testssl.sh** 目前看起来更“完整”，暗示其功能覆盖面可能比 **sslyze** 更广或更成熟。
  
• **输出质量的比较**：[peblos] 提到 **sslyze** 的输出不如 **testssl.sh** 那么有条理，并且在一些检查项中出现了错误信息，这可能是 **sslyze** 需要改进的地方。

争议焦点：
• **可读性和错误处理**：目前争议的焦点在于 **sslyze** 的输出可读性较差以及在某些检查中出现的 tracebacks 问题，这影响了用户体验。这可能是 **sslyze** 相对于 **testssl.sh** 的一个劣势。

总结：讨论围绕 **testssl.sh** 和 **sslyze** 在 SSL/TLS 测试中的表现展开，主要比较了输出质量、工具完整性和错误处理能力。用户 [peblos] 倾向于 **testssl.sh**，但对 **sslyze** 的潜在优势持开放态度。

SSLyze
SSLyze is a fast and powerful SSL/TLS scanning tool and Python library.
SSLyze can analyze the SSL/TLS configuration of a server by connecting to it, in order to ensure that it uses strong
encryption settings (certificate, cipher suites, elliptic curves, etc.), and that it is not vulnerable to known TLS
attacks (Heartbleed, ROBOT, OpenSSL CCS injection, etc.).
Key features
Focus on speed and reliability: SSLyze is a battle-tested tool that is used to reliably scan
hundreds of thousands
of servers every day.
Easy to operationalize: SSLyze can be directly run from CI/CD, in order to continuously check a server against
Mozilla's recommended TLS configuration.
Fully documented
Python API
to run scans directly from any
Python application, such as a function deployed to AWS Lambda.
Support for scanning non-HTTP servers including SMTP, XMPP, LDAP, POP, IMAP, RDP, Postgres and FTP servers.
Results of a scan can easily be saved to a JSON file for later processing.
And much more!
Quick start
On Windows, Linux (x86 or x64) and macOS, SSLyze can be installed directly via pip:
$ pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
$ pip install --upgrade sslyze
$ python -m sslyze www.yahoo.com www.google.com "[2607:f8b0:400a:807::2004]:443"
It can also be used via Docker:
$ docker run --rm -it nablac0d3/sslyze:6.1.0 www.google.com
Lastly, a pre-compiled Windows executable can be downloaded from
the Releases
page
.
Python API Documentation
A sample script describing how to use the SSLyze's Python API is available at
./api_sample.py
.
Full documentation for SSLyze's Python API is
available here
.
Usage as a CI/CD step
By default, SSLyze will check the server's scan results against Mozilla's recommended
"intermediate" TLS
configuration
, and will return a non-zero exit code if the server
is not compliant.
$ python -m sslyze mozilla.com
Checking results against Mozilla's "intermediate" configuration. See https://ssl-config.mozilla.org/ for more details.
mozilla.com:443: OK - Compliant.
The Mozilla configuration to check against can be configured via
--mozilla_config={old, intermediate, modern}
:
$ python -m sslyze --mozilla_config=modern mozilla.com
Checking results against Mozilla's "modern" configuration. See https://ssl-config.mozilla.org/ for more details.
mozilla.com:443: FAILED - Not compliant.
* certificate_types: Deployed certificate types are {'rsa'}, should have at least one of {'ecdsa'}.
* certificate_signatures: Deployed certificate signatures are {'sha256WithRSAEncryption'}, should have at least one of {'ecdsa-with-SHA512', 'ecdsa-with-SHA256', 'ecdsa-with-SHA384'}.
* tls_versions: TLS versions {'TLSv1.2'} are supported, but should be rejected.
* ciphers: Cipher suites {'TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384', 'TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256', 'TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256'} are supported, but should be rejected.
This can be used to easily run an SSLyze scan as a CI/CD step.
Development environment
To setup a development environment:
$ pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
$ pip install -e .
$ pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
The tests can then be run using:
$ invoke test

data.title: Silicon Valley, Halt and Catch Fire, and How Microserfdom Ate the World (2015)
data.author: Apocryphon
data.article_summary:
《Microserfs》是道格拉斯·柯普兰（Douglas Coupland）于20年前出版的小说，讲述了年轻程序员在软件开发过程中的精神渴望和琐碎活动，展现了他们从微软转战创业的生活。尽管该书是早期描写北美科技公司和初创企业文化的先驱之一，但过去二十年中并未引起太多关注。尽管曾有计划将其改编为电影和电视剧，但都未实现，唯一存在的改编是马修·派瑞录制的缩写有声书。

小说的主角丹尼尔是26岁的微软员工，通过日记记录了对职业和存在的焦虑，如对生产力不足的恐惧、对公司福利的担忧等。他和室友们离开微软前往硅谷，追求由同事迈克尔提出的新科技项目，这一过程让他们重新审视自己与身体、生活的关系。小说不仅探讨了科技和创业，更关注知识工作者在精神和肉体之间的割裂感。书中提到的软件Oop!预示了类似Minecraft的创新。这部作品源于《连线》杂志的报道，结合了虚构与现实。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：1990年代的科技文化及其当代回响

不同观点：
• [markus_zhang] 认为1990年代的梦想是将工作与自我本性融为一体，追求一种完美的、近乎“神性”的状态。这与工作狂不同，工作狂源于逃避过去的不幸，而这种追求是一种有意识的自我进化和突破。

• [ryandrake] 提到《Microserfs》一书精准捕捉了1990年代科技行业的精神，尤其是早期科技从业者的存在焦虑。尽管时代变迁，但书中的许多内容在今天依然具有相关性。

• [Animats] 认为计算技术在成为广告行业的一部分之前更为纯粹，暗示现代科技被商业化侵蚀。

• [jgord] 提出当前正处于新一轮技术变革的起点，类似于1990年代的互联网 boom。他认为不需要等到AGI（通用人工智能）出现，现有技术已经能够推动巨大的经济增长。然而，目前风险投资与初创企业之间的资本匹配存在问题，需要更多的天使投资人参与。

• [vlark] 怀念已停刊的Grantland，认为其曾是网络上最好的写作平台之一，并对ESPN结束该项目表示遗憾。

• [kelseydh] 强调在科技趋势上升期的兴奋感与不确定性，尽管知道技术发展的方向，但很难抓住机会。

• [udev4096] 对《Halt and Catch Fire》在第二季后未被继续评论表示失望，认为该剧在每一季都有所提升。

• [azinman2] 表示《Microserfs》是他成长过程中最喜欢的一本书，并计划重读以检验其在现代的适应性。

• [low_tech_love] 赞赏文章顶部的插图，认为其美丽且具有人文气息。

• [timewizard] 引用《Microserfs》中的描述，认为1990年代的硅谷在史蒂夫·乔布斯被放逐和网络亿万富翁俱乐部出现之前是一个“没有国王的王国”，那是他记忆中最快乐的时光。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及多个1990年代的文化符号，如《Microserfs》、Grantland等，反映出对那个时代科技与文化交织的怀念。
- 关于现代科技投资与初创企业发展的讨论，特别是天使投资的重要性，成为新的关注点。
- 争议的焦点在于现代计算技术的商业化是否损害了其本质，以及当前是否处于类似于1990年代的技术变革时期。

43551338.article_content:
Start-up Costs: ‘Silicon Valley,’ ‘Halt and Catch Fire,’ and How Microserfdom Ate the World
Mario Zucca
TV
June 19, 2015
by
Alex Pappademas
Facebook
Twitter
Print
Douglas Coupland’s novel
Microserfs
is about the spiritual yearnings and time-frittering activities of youngish coders immersed in the drudgery of the software-development process, and how those activities become an expression of those yearnings. It was published 20 years ago this month, which as far as I’m aware makes it the earliest significant stab by a fiction writer at the Great North American Tech-Company/Start-up Novel. It predates Po Bronson’s
The First $20 Million Is Always the Hardest
, Thomas Pynchon’s
Bleeding Edge
, Dave Eggers’s
The Circle
, numerous other neuroman-à-clefs, score-settling pseudomemoirs and murder-dot-com whodunits,
1
as well as tech-sector TV shows like
Silicon Valley
and
Halt and Catch Fire
, serials that pick up where the novels leave off.
Coupland’s evocation of the inner lives of programmers turning entrepreneur in mid-’90s Redmond and Palo Alto should, in theory, enjoy the reputational equivalent of what marketers call first-mover advantage. But I’m not sure it does. Nobody’s talked about it much in the last two decades. Coupland’s most famous book is still his first one, which named a generation (or two) and made Coupland (b. 1961) the most visible and visibly reluctant spokesman for his peer group pre–Kurt Cobain.
Universal Pictures bought
the film rights to
Microserfs
two years after it was published, and
IMDb insists
a low-budget movie did get made in 2011, but there’s no trace of it elsewhere on the Internet.
2
Nor did it become a Fox TV show, despite a mention in
Wired
that one was in the works. Maybe the overall bagginess of the book’s epistolary narrative stymied potential screenwriters; maybe adapting a book whose first and arguably most important section is about the office culture of a nonfictional household-name software company then run by one of the richest men in America presented insurmountable legal challenges. Had the TV show taken place among the cubicles of “GloboCom” and featured characters speaking in reverent tones of their omniscient CEO “Gil Yates,” something would probably have been lost. As it stands, the only extant
Microserfs
adaptation I know of is the abridged audiobook, read by
Friends
star (and soon-to-be
Windows 95 shill
) Matthew Perry. I have it on cassette tape; it is maybe the most ’90s object I have ever owned, a curio as totemic as a lock of Alanis Morissette’s hair preserved in a flannel-swaddled vial of Crystal Pepsi.
Microserfs
is written as a series of entries from the PowerBook journal of a 26-year-old named Daniel, who when the story begins is making $26,000 a year as a “bug checker” in Building Seven
3
of Microsoft’s Redmond campus, living in a $235-a-month group house with other Microsoft employees, and dealing with anxieties professional and existential
:
[F]ear of not producing enough; fear of not finding a little white-with-red-printing stock option envelope in the pigeonhole; fear of losing the sensation of actually making something anymore; fear about the slow erosion of perks within the company; fear that the growth years will never return again; fear that the bottom line is the only thing that really drives the process; fear of disposability…
He has trouble sleeping and maintaining relationships and struggles with a sense of alienation from the physical world. “I feel like my body is a station wagon in which I drive my brain around,” he writes, “like a suburban mother taking the kids to hockey practice.” There’s a case to be made that this — the disconnect between the mental and the physical as experienced by members of a caste of golden-handcuffed knowledge workers, and the possibility of greater harmony between car and driver, consciousness-wise — is the book’s real subject, rather than Microsoft or “tech” or start-up-house life. When Daniel and most of his housemates leave Washington and Microsoft for Silicon Valley to work on a Next Big Thing hatched by their programming-genius coworker Michael, the move precipitates a kind of spring thaw within the crew. Everyone renegotiates their relationship with their body in one way or another: characters take up shiatsu massage, come out of the closet, come to grips with childhood eating disorders, dress experimentally, grow their hair out, fuck and procreate, and work up the courage to meet their Net-chat crushes offline. The post-corporate work environment becomes a context in which these former brains-in-a-jar learn to feel the sun on their skin again — while building a revolutionary new software application called Oop!, which allows users to do object-oriented programming by manipulating Lego-like bricks and seems to anticipate Minecraft more than a little bit.
Microserfs
was fiction grounded in embedded reporting; it began its life as a magazine story for
Wired
. More than one outlet had offered to send Coupl
43551338.article_summary:
《Microserfs》是道格拉斯·柯普兰（Douglas Coupland）于20年前出版的小说，讲述了年轻程序员在软件开发过程中的精神渴望和琐碎活动，展现了他们从微软转战创业的生活。尽管该书是早期描写北美科技公司和初创企业文化的先驱之一，但过去二十年中并未引起太多关注。尽管曾有计划将其改编为电影和电视剧，但都未实现，唯一存在的改编是马修·派瑞录制的缩写有声书。

小说的主角丹尼尔是26岁的微软员工，通过日记记录了对职业和存在的焦虑，如对生产力不足的恐惧、对公司福利的担忧等。他和室友们离开微软前往硅谷，追求由同事迈克尔提出的新科技项目，这一过程让他们重新审视自己与身体、生活的关系。小说不仅探讨了科技和创业，更关注知识工作者在精神和肉体之间的割裂感。书中提到的软件Oop!预示了类似Minecraft的创新。这部作品源于《连线》杂志的报道，结合了虚构与现实。

data.title: The timeless genius of a Atari developer and his swimming salmon masterpiece
data.author: myth_drannon
data.article_summary: 《Salmon Run》是1982年比尔·威廉姆斯为Atari 800开发的一款独特游戏，象征着在逆境中奋斗的生活。玩家扮演一条逆流而上的鲑鱼，躲避岩石、瀑布和捕食者，最终与上游的雌鲑鱼产卵。这款游戏不仅在音效设计上突破了8位硬件的限制，逼真地模拟了水流声，还融入了威廉姆斯自身与囊性纤维化斗争的深刻意义。游戏通过简单的像素画面和出色的声音设计，创造出独特的自然氛围，成为对生活艰难的隐喻。威廉姆斯对Atari声音芯片的精妙运用，使他成为当时音效设计的先锋，甚至影响了后来的游戏开发者。

In 1982, while most game developers were busy with space invaders and maze ghosts,
Bill Williams
created something far more profound: a game about swimming upstream against impossible odds.
Salmon Run
for the Atari 800 served as a powerful metaphor for life itself, one that resonates even more deeply when you learn about the creator's own struggles with cystic fibrosis.
As a kid
growing up
in the 1980s with an
Atari 800 home computer
, I discovered this hidden gem in our family's game collection, and it soon became a favorite. What struck me most—and what still amazes me today—was its incredible audio design, creating water sounds that seemed impossible for 8-bit hardware. But
Salmon Run
was about far more than impressive audio.
In the game, you play as Sam the Salmon, swimming upriver to spawn with a female salmon waiting upstream. You control your speed while dodging obstacles like rocks, waterfalls, and riverbanks, moving left to right and leaping from the water. And predators—bears, fishermen, and birds—are constantly trying to eat you.
Gameplay of
Salmon Run
for the Atari 8-bit computer family.
The "swimming against the current" gameplay isn't just clever game design. Williams spent his life navigating his own treacherous currents—hospital visits, treatments, and the constant struggle just to breathe. His personal battle with cystic fibrosis, characterized by chronic pain, infused
Salmon Run
with authentic meaning that transcends its simple pixels.
In a world grappling with anxiety, uncertainty, and relentless pressures,
Salmon Run
feels especially timely to me. While not all of us face challenges of Williams' magnitude, I am sure anyone reading can attest that life isn't easy. It isn't a passive process—it's a deliberate, ongoing work of labor. We constantly get pushed back by the current. And all the while, both metaphorical and literal bears are trying to eat us.
The Atari 800 home computer, as seen in an Atari promotional brochure.
Credit:
Atari
In a way, the inherent struggles and dangers of life make the ostensibly non-violent gameplay of
Salmon Run
even more enjoyable. Unlike most Atari games, you're not blasting aliens or dodging maze ghosts; instead, you're navigating a natural, down-to-earth challenge.
I'm not alone in my appreciation for this gem. As one Atari Mania reviewer named JSUK
wrote
: "Bill Williams' first game shows why he is so revered. The concept is simple but the execution is perfect. Controls are responsive, the sound effects replicate ocean waves better than you'd imagine the A8 hardware could, and there's even a little animated reward after each level. Magical."
The digital rapids of sound design
For fun, I have recently been developing a modern computer game for myself set in the rainy, natural outdoors, and I was trying to figure out the best way to make rain sound effects. That had me looking back at
Salmon Run
. How did Williams achieve what he did? According to the
Digital Antiquarian
, it turns out that Williams' sound effects in
Salmon Run
were so highly regarded that he was asked to write a regular "
Atari Sound
" column for Softline Magazine in the early 1980s.
The water sounds in
Salmon Run
weren't just impressive for their realism—they showed a deep understanding of the Atari's sound capabilities. In his Softline columns, Williams explained how noise could create a wide range of natural sounds, from "the soothing sounds of wind and surf" to "the pitter-patter of raindrops on a window." This wasn't just random beeping—it required careful manipulation of the
Atari's POKEY sound chip
and its various noise patterns, which generate certain frequencies to make white noise, pink noise, and brown noise (what audio engineers call "
colors of noise
").
By controlling both the randomness and the frequency range of these sounds, he could create everything from gentle burbles to rushing cascades. "We live in an audible universe," Williams wrote, explaining why sound design mattered so much in games. "The correct blend of the visual and auditory makes good games good."
A photo of the author's brother and the next-door neighbor playing Atari 800 games circa 1985.
Credit:
Benj Edwards
The Atari POKEY chip might seem primitive by today's standards—with just four 8-bit sound channels—but in Williams' hands, it sang like a mountain stream. While many developers at the time settled for simple beeps and boops, Williams coaxed naturalistic environmental sounds from the silicon that modern audio designers, working with gigabytes of sampled audio, would still appreciate.
While popular memory of retro sound tends to fixate on the
chiptune melodies
of the NES era, Williams was pioneering environmental sound design years earlier. The rushing water in S
almon Run
doesn't just sound realistic—it creates genuine atmosphere, pulling players into its pixela

data.title: Neuralatex: A machine learning library written in pure LATEX
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为Neuralatex的机器学习库，它完全用LaTeX编写，可以在LaTeX文档中定义神经网络架构、损失函数、训练数据和超参数，并在编译时训练模型、运行实验和生成图表。该库解决了可重现性问题，将代码、数据和实验全部包含在LaTeX源文件中，使Overleaf成为免费的云计算服务。Neuralatex基于MicroGrad实现，支持反向自动微分，尽管代码较长，但在小规模任务上表现良好。作者还提出了WIL和SCOMISCOP两个新指标，以衡量机器学习库在LaTeX中的实现程度。未来计划包括支持加速器、扩展功能以及商业化。

43551700.article_content:
A machine learning library written in pure LaTeX
James. A. D. Gardner
,
Will Rowan
,
William. A. P. Smith
University of York
Paper (and source code!)
Source code (and paper!)
Abstract
Neuralatex is a scalar values-based auto-grad library similar to
MicroGrad
but written entirely in latex! As part of your latex
document you can specify the architecture of a neural network and
loss functions, how to generate or load training data, and specify
training hyperparameters and experiments. When the document
is compiled, the latex compiler will generate or load training data,
train the network, run experiments and generate figures. Training
debug output can be written to the latex compiler log or included
as part of the paper itself.
Why?
Ideal Language:
LaTeX offers macros instead of variables, comma-separated strings instead of arrays, and flexible loop options like
pgfplotsforeachungrouped
.
Self-Contained Paper:
Solves reproducibility by including all code, data, and experiments in the LaTeX source, executable during compilation.
Overleaf as Compute:
Turns
Overleaf
into a free cloud compute service for training models.
Small-Scale Focus:
arXiv’s 50MB limit encourages small datasets and models, leveling the playing field.
Unified Workflow:
Combines paper writing and coding in one LaTeX environment, reducing context switching.
No Git Needed:
Links to arXiv source files replace GitHub, eliminating pesky version control hassles.
Implementation
Our implementation is heavily based on micrograd
MicroGrad
, although with a better choice of implementation language!
Like MicroGrad, Neuralatex implements backpropagation (reverse-mode autodiff) over a dynamically-constructed DAG which can implement arbitrarily complex neural networks.
Unlike MicroGrad (which comprises around 150 lines of python), our autograd engine requires nearly 700 lines of pure latex and the neural network library around 400!
We estimate that this means Neuralatex is around 700% better. Neuralatex is object oriented using the TiKZ PGF module
oo
.
Getting the gradients of a computation is as simple as calling .backward() !
\pgfoonew \x=new Value(2.5,{},'',0)
\x.show()
\pgfoonew \y=new Value(0.3,{},'',0)
\y.show()
\x.multiply(\y,z)
\z.show()
\z.backward()
\x.show()
\y.show()
This prints:
Value(self: 1, data: 2.5, grad: 0.0, prev: , next: , op: ", isparam: 0, GC: 0.0)
Value(self: 2, data: 0.3, grad: 0.0, prev: , next: , op: ", isparam: 0, GC: 0.0)
Value(self: 3, data: 0.75, grad: 0.0, prev: 1,2, next: , op: *, isparam: 0, GC: 0.0)
Value(self: 1, data: 2.5, grad: 0.3, prev: , next: 3, op: ", isparam: 0, GC: 1.0)
Value(self: 2, data: 0.3, grad: 2.5, prev: , next: 3, op: ", isparam: 0, GC: 1.0)
And defining and calling an MLP is easy too!
\input{engine.tex}
% Create two Value objects to store input values
\pgfoonew \x=new Value(1.0,{},'',0)
\pgfoonew \y=new Value(-1.0,{},'',0)
% Store the object IDs of the input Values in a list
\x.get id(\inputIDx)
\y.get id(\inputIDy)
\edef\templist{\inputIDx,\inputIDy}
% Define the MLP
\pgfoonew \mlp=new MLP(2,{4,4,1})
% Forward pass through MLP
\mlp.forward(\templist,output)
Demo
To demonstrate the power of our library we trained a small MLP to classify
the two classes of the nonlinear, 2D spiral dataset.
Training for 35 epochs on a dataset of 100 2D points
(i.e. compiling the latex document) took only 48 hours
on a Macbook Pro 2.4GHz Quad-Core! The document
was compiled using TeXShop and the Macbook got very
hot. We could have trained for more epochs but we thought it was obvious it was going to converge to zero loss and perfect
test set performance so we didn’t feel the need to.
Training Dataset
Eval Dataset Results (86% Accuracy)
Additionally we propose two new metrics. The
Written in Latex
(WIL) metric is the proportion of source code
of a machine learning library written in LaTeX and the
Source code of method in source code of paper
(SCOMISCOP) metric
is the proportion of the source code of a method that is contained within the source code of the paper. See how Neuralatex is
state-of-the-art in both metrics!

Support for arbitrary accelerators, GPUs, TPUs, Hadron Colliders! Lets get that compile time down!

Neuralatex is not just the world’s best and only fully reproducible machine learning library, but also the future substrate of all computation!

data.article_summary: Tailscale宣布为其Enterprise计划增加对Plan 9操作系统的支持。通过集成WireGuard技术，Plan 9用户可以实现全球范围的无缝、安全连接，如同在同一局域网内，且无需手动配置。该集成支持全局命名空间、无密码SSH连接、ACL配置以及Plan 9的原生IPv6支持。Tailscale对Plan 9的实现免费开放，并提供企业支持服务。现有用户可以通过多种方式获取和安装Tailscale，包括使用ftpfs或从CVS服务器获取源代码。Tailscale还提供了基于网页的模拟器和QEMU环境供评估。更多详情可访问tailscale.com/plan9。

with Plan 9’s
ndb(7)
.
Use
Plan 9's native IPv6 support
,
just approved
as a draft standard, or fall back to legacy IPv4 and rely on direct connections via Tailscale's stopgap NAT traversal support that will obviously be retired once the short IPv6 transition is complete.
Early reactions to Tailscale Subsystem for Plan 9 have been overwhelmingly positive:
“
Using Tailscale with Plan 9 makes it easy to connect to the Bell Labs networks from anywhere, even my college dorm room
.”, said Plan 9 torchbearer
Russ Cox
. “
It feels like the future has arrived
.”
"You want a quote for this astonishing event. That's awkward."
, said the
iconic
Peter J. Weinberger, facing an uncharacteristic loss for words.
"Please tell me this isn't why the Tailscale logo has nine dots"
, said
{tails,scales}.txt
curator emerita
Charlotte Brandhorst-Satzkorn
.
Pricing
Rather than a bespoke license that might hinder the community, our lawyers have approved making
Tailscale for Plan 9 available free of charge
under an
OSI
-approved, restriction-free license.
Tailscale Enterprise Support for Tailscale for Plan 9 is additionally now available for customers with
suitably sized
containers of cash.
Availability
Tailscale for Plan 9 is
available today
. Existing Plan 9 users can mount the binaries into their namespace at
/n/ftp/tailscale*
using
ftpfs
-t -a anon ftp.plan9.ts.net
or get the source code from a
local CVS server
. When building from source, for best results use
GOOS=plan9
,
GOARCH=386
, and Go
HEAD
or
Tailscale’s Enterprise Go
.
For users of legacy operating systems, two evaluation options are available: 1)
a web-based emulator of Tailscale Enterprise Plan 9
if you’ve been waiting to be able to SSH from your laptop into an OS running in your browser on your laptop, 2) a
qemu environment
. Alternatively, download the
16 MB disk image
and use the hypervisor of your choice.
Be aware that like the
twelve-fingered pianist
in the recent hit
Gattaca
, Plan 9
requires
a three button mouse. Users lacking the requisite mice buttons will need to use modifier keys while clicking.
For more information, see
tailscale.com/plan9
.

data.title: Nuclear power is officially a clean energy source in Colorado
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 科罗拉多州通过了1040号众议院法案，将核能列入该州的清洁能源资源名单，为未来核项目提供特殊资金机会。尽管核能被视为无化石燃料电力的一种创新来源，但也引发了对公共健康和环境的担忧，特别是核废料的储存问题。该法案的提案人强调，它并不强制要求使用核能，只是使其成为可行选项。科罗拉多西北部正在探讨建立核废料储存设施的可能性，当地对此态度不一。支持者认为核能是减少碳排放的重要途径，而反对者则担心其历史上的安全隐患和放射性废料处理问题。法案的通过反映了在摆脱化石燃料和维持电网稳定之间的艰难平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：核能是否应被视为清洁能源，以及与其他清洁能源（如太阳能）的比较

不同观点：
• [natmaka] 对核能的“清洁性”提出质疑，通过引用洛基弗拉茨工厂（Rocky Flats Plant）的放射性污染历史，暗示核能并非真正的清洁能源。该评论侧重于核能设施可能带来的长期环境污染问题。

• [more_corn] 认为核能在运行过程中是清洁的，但承认在退役和处理核废料方面存在问题。该评论提出，虽然核能作为一种能源来源有其优点，但其高昂的建设成本、长时间的建造周期以及潜在的安全隐患使得其在经济和环境上的可行性存疑。此外，评论提倡优先发展分布式太阳能和储能技术，认为这是更直接且可持续的解决方案，只有在太阳能等技术达到回报递减点后才应考虑小型核电站。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于核能是否应被视为清洁能源。一方关注核能的历史污染记录，另一方则承认其在运行中的清洁性，但质疑其全生命周期的经济和环境成本。

• [more_corn] 进一步扩展讨论，提出了分布式投资和增加电网稳定性的优点，并将太阳能与核能进行比较，认为太阳能是更优的优先选择。

• 小型核电站被提及作为未来可能的补充能源选项，但这是在太阳能等其他清洁能源达到其极限之后才被考虑。

Original Reporting
The Trust Project
Original Reporting
This article contains firsthand information gathered by reporters. This includes directly interviewing sources and analyzing primary source documents.
Workers pose with a new train car designed to carry highly-radioactive nuclear waste from power plants around the country. An economic development group in northwest Colorado is entertaining the idea of pursuing a storage facility for the waste. (U.S. Department of Energy photo)
Nuclear power — an innovative source of fossil-free power potential, or a radioactive risk that threatens public health and the environment, depending on whom you ask — is back on the table in Colorado.
House Bill 1040
, which adds nuclear energy to the state’s list of clean energy resources, was signed into law Monday by Gov. Jared Polis.
The state defines clean energy as geothermal, solar, small hydroelectricity, wind and hydrogen energy. The law essentially tacks the words “and nuclear” onto the end of that list, opening up future nuclear projects to
special funding
opportunities.
But nuclear energy
has a fraught history
that left the bill’s many opponents wondering about Colorado’s definition of clean.
Nuclear energy requires uranium, a radioactive element that is mined and milled for nuclear power and weapons production. Uranium production in the U.S. takes place
primarily on public and tribal lands
in the West.
☀️ READ MORE
Mistrust bubbles up as nuclear waste storage talks come to rural Colorado
4:10 AM MST on Feb 6, 2025
9:04 AM MST on Feb 6, 2025
Replacing mining with nuclear waste? Northwestern Colorado has mixed feelings about how to save the economy.
3:59 AM MST on Jan 29, 2025
9:05 PM MST on Jan 28, 2025
10 years after the last uranium speculator left Cañon City, an Australian company is on the hunt
4:47 AM MST on Jan 17, 2024
10:11 AM MST on Jan 17, 2024
There’s also the question of nuclear waste, once power has been generated: where to put it, and who is responsible for keeping it secure.
The bill’s sponsors dodged specific questions about how waste would be stored by pointing out that the bill does not promise any nuclear development, it only makes those projects a more economically viable option. Nuclear energy is not banned in Colorado, and
nuclear power plants have been proposed
as recently as last fall.
“House Bill 1040 is not — is not — a mandate, nor does it require that a city or a utility use nuclear energy,” Sen. Larry Liston, a Colorado Springs Republican, said during a Senate committee hearing March 10. “It only adds nuclear as a recognized form of clean energy.”
Liston has proposed a similar bill twice before,
in 2023
and 2024
. Neither measure made it out of its first chamber. This year, though, Liston was joined by Sen. Dylan Roberts, a Frisco Democrat, and Reps. Alex Valdez, a Denver Democrat, and Ty Winter, a Republican from Trinidad, in the House.
The driving force of the newfound bipartisan support is the increasingly urgent issue of moving the state away from fossil fuels while maintaining a stable electrical grid and avoiding layoffs for large portions of Colorado’s workforce.
A
plan to create a national nuclear waste depository
is being explored in Roberts’ district in the northwestern corner of the state.
Roberts told the chamber that he would not push nuclear production over solar, wind and geothermal.
“But numbers don’t lie,” Roberts said. “We will never get to 100% carbon-free energy with just wind and solar.”
Between coal-fired and carbon-free
Nuclear energy has been in and out of fashion since the 1950s. Throughout the ’50s and ’60s, the U.S. went on a nuclear reactor building spree — by the end of the 1960s, there were more than 50 reactors under construction or built in the U.S.
But the industry started to experience a slowdown in the 1970s, and the
Three Mile Island meltdown
at a nuclear power plant in Pennsylvania in 1979 ground things to a halt. Costs went up, regulations piled on, construction contracts were paused or canceled altogether.
In recent years, the intensity of climate change and pressure to shift away from fossil fuel use has created a nuclear power resurgence among clean energy groups. In June, TerraPower, the nuclear energy company founded by Bill Gates, broke ground in Wyoming for a new generation of nuclear reactor, which uses a lower pressure system than the traditional reactors built around the U.S.
Last year, global energy demand rose faster than ever before, largely due to high temperatures, widespread electric vehicle use and the growth of data centers in the U.S. and China, according to
a report by the International Energy Agency
released in March.

data.title: First Retinal Treatment to Restore Damaged Vision
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 韩国科学技术院（KAIST）金振宇教授团队开发了一种通过抑制Prox1蛋白恢复视网膜再生能力的技术，从而治疗视力损伤。研究发现，Prox1蛋白抑制哺乳动物 Müller 胶质细胞的脱分化，导致视网膜无法再生。团队使用中和抗体阻止Prox1的作用，成功在实验鼠视网膜中实现了长期的神经再生和视力恢复。该技术为目前无法治愈的退行性视网膜疾病患者带来了希望，相关治疗方法预计2028年进入临床试验。研究成果发表于《Nature Communications》。

Prof. Kim Jin-woo's Team Blocks Prox1 Protein Inhibiting Retinal Regeneration
A research team of the Korea Advanced Institute of Science & Technology (KAIST) has developed a technology that can treat damaged vision by regenerating the retina. The image depicts the mechanism of inducing retinal regeneration by inhibiting the movement of PROX1. (Photo courtesy of KAIST)
A research team of the Korea Advanced Institute of Science & Technology (KAIST) has developed the world's first retinal disease treatment that can restore damaged vision.
KAIST announced on March 30 that Prof. Kim Jin-woo's team from the Department of Biological Sciences has developed a treatment method that can restore vision through retinal nerve regeneration.
The team successfully induced neural regeneration and vision recovery in retinal tissue by administering a substance that blocks the "Prox1" protein, which inhibits retinal regeneration, into the eyes of disease model mice. The effects lasted for more than six months.
This is the first case in the world to induce long-term neural regeneration in mammalian retinas and is expected to bring hope to patients with degenerative retinal diseases, for which no treatment currently exists.
There is currently no treatment to restore the retina and vision of patients with damage.
Research on ectothermic animals like fish, which have active retinal regeneration, shows that fish have the ability to generate new nerve cells by dedifferentiating Müller glia cells in the retina into neural progenitor cells when retinal damage occurs. However, in mammals like humans, this function is lost, resulting in permanent damage as retinal regeneration does not occur.
In this study, Prof. Kim's team identified the Prox1 protein as a factor that inhibits the dedifferentiation of mammalian Müller glia cells. Prox1 is a protein generated in the nerve cells of neural tissues such as the retina, hippocampus, and spinal cord, which suppresses the division of neural stem cells and induces differentiation into nerve cells.
The research team discovered that the Prox1 protein accumulates in the Müller glia of damaged mouse retinas but not in the Müller glia of fish, where regeneration is active.
They also identified that the Prox1 in Müller glia is not internally generated but is secreted by surrounding nerve cells that fail to degrade it, which is then taken up by Müller glia.
The research team developed a method to restore the neural regeneration ability of Müller glia by removing Prox1 secreted from nerve cells externally before it reaches Müller glia.
Prof. Kim Jin-woo (center) poses for a photo together with Dr. Lee Eun-jeong (right) from Celliaz and KAIST doctoral student Kim Moo-sung. (Photo courtesy of KAIST)
The research team explained, "The PROX1 protein secreted from damaged retinal nerve cells moves to Müller glia, inhibiting dedifferentiation into neural progenitor cells and neural regeneration. By capturing external PROX1 with a neutralizing antibody against PROX1, we can prevent its movement to Müller glia, restart the dedifferentiation and neural regeneration process of Müller glia cells, and restore retinal function."
This method utilizes antibodies that bind to Prox1, discovered by Celliaz Inc., a startup founded by Prof. Kim as a lab venture (a KAIST faculty startup).
In particular, it was proven that when the Prox1 neutralizing antibody was administered to disease-modeling mouse retinas, active neural regeneration occurred, and when delivered in the form of a gene therapy to congenital retinal degenerative disease mouse retinas, continuous generation of nerve cells and vision recovery were maintained for over six months.
Celliaz is currently developing a retinal regeneration-inducing treatment based on these research results to apply to various degenerative retinal diseases, with the goal of entering clinical trials by 2028.
This research, with Dr. Lee Eun-jeong from Celliaz and KAIST doctoral student Kim Moo-sung as co-first authors, was published online in the international journal "Nature Communications" on March 26 (Paper title: Restoration of retinal regenerative potential of Müller glia by disrupting intercellular Prox1 transfer).
Dr. Lee stated, "The work to improve the efficacy of the Prox1 neutralizing antibody is complete, and after evaluating its vision restoration efficacy and safety using various animals, we will proceed with administration to retinal disease patients," adding, "We will strive to make a practical contribution to patients at risk of blindness without appropriate treatment."

data.author: LouisLazaris

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网页构建工具及其相关域名管理、SEO影响和开发者体验

不同观点：
• 观点一：网页构建工具是面向普通消费者的商品化产品。jayturley指出，这些工具主要是为了让用户自行构建网站，属于"获取网站"的初步商品化阶段。它们对于开发者而言，比开源工具（如WordPress、Laravel、Hugo等）更难扩展，且由于是封闭生态，迁移成本较高。
   
• 观点二：域名管理和所有权清晰。jayturley解释，这些工具提供商作为注册商，与其它注册商无异。用户可以在不同注册商之间自由转移域名，且在注册期内，用户拥有域名的实际控制权，工具提供商并不拥有用户的域名。

• 观点三：SEO优化依赖于用户自身的努力。jayturley提到，这些网页构建工具不会带来显著的SEO惩罚，但与所有网站一样，用户需要自行进行SEO优化工作，才能达到理想效果。

补充讨论：
• 关于开发者工具的选择，jayturley明确表示更偏好于开源工具，因为这些工具允许开发者自由改进、扩展，甚至可以通过实验性的编码进行探索，而网页构建工具则限制较多。

• 争议焦点：网页构建工具的封闭性和难以迁移的问题是讨论中的一个争议点。一方面，这些工具为没有技术背景的用户提供了便捷的建站途径，但另一方面，对于有技术需求的开发者而言，它们的扩展性和灵活性不足，且一旦使用，用户会面临较高的迁移成本。

• 观点二：域名管理和所有权清晰。jayturley解释，这些工具提供商作为注册商，与其它注册商无异。用户可以在不同注册商之间自由转移域名，且在注册期内，用户拥有域名的实际控制权，工具提供商并不拥有用户的域名。

• 观点三：SEO优化依赖于用户自身的努力。jayturley提到，这些网页构建工具不会带来显著的SEO惩罚，但与所有网站一样，用户需要自行进行SEO优化工作，才能达到理想效果。

补充讨论：
• 关于开发者工具的选择，jayturley明确表示更偏好于开源工具，因为这些工具允许开发者自由改进、扩展，甚至可以通过实验性的编码进行探索，而网页构建工具则限制较多。

• 争议焦点：网页构建工具的封闭性和难以迁移的问题是讨论中的一个争议点。一方面，这些工具为没有技术背景的用户提供了便捷的建站途径，但另一方面，对于有技术需求的开发者而言，它们的扩展性和灵活性不足，且一旦使用，用户会面临较高的迁移成本。

data.title: Why I run FreeBSD for my home servers (2024)
data.author: psxuaw
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了2024年Linux作为桌面操作系统的优异表现，尤其是在EndeavourOS发行版上的体验，指出其在日常使用中的良好表现，包括游戏、程序安装和设备连接等方面。然而，作为服务器操作系统，Linux特别是基于RedHat的系统，因SystemD的复杂性和过多的抽象层（如Docker和Kubernetes）而显得混乱，增加了故障排查的难度。文章批评了SystemD导致的系统复杂性和可靠性问题，并对比了不同Linux发行版在包管理和网络配置上的差异。作者还称赞了FreeBSD在生产环境中的简单性和稳定性，认为其无重大变更的升级体验更适合专业使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FreeBSD与Linux（尤其是systemd相关）的比较，以及在不同应用场景下的优缺点讨论。

不同观点：
• nine_k认为，systemd、Kubernetes等并不是必须的，用户有其他选择（如Void Linux），且容器技术并不复杂，类似于BSD的jails。FreeBSD的优势在于ZFS、内核和网络栈等，而非因为一些人提到的Linux常见问题。
• solid_fuel强调FreeBSD的管理工具稳定，不常变化，如`ifconfig`长期保持一致，减少了管理员的困扰。相比之下，Linux的管理工具变化较频繁，更新时可能导致习惯的工具被移除或改变。
• asveikau选择FreeBSD的主要原因是ZFS，并从哲学上更倾向于*BSD系统，同时也在使用OpenBSD和Linux。
• aeblyve引用了Schneier的博客，讨论了“廉价复杂性”问题，认为systemd虽然增加了复杂性，但也解决了许多问题，是技术进步的一部分。
• carlhjerpe对systemd持积极态度，认为它适合大多数人，不认同对systemd的抱怨。
• rollcat对FreeBSD有复杂的感受，认为其在某些方面优于Linux（如ZFS体验、man页面等），但在某些方面又显得混乱（如多个防火墙、配置文件分散等）。相比OpenBSD，FreeBSD在桌面和使用便捷性上较为落后。
• lunarlull认为，BSD的优势不再明显，许多核心性能改进首先出现在Linux上，最终选择多取决于用户偏好，并推荐了Alpine、Void等无systemd的Linux发行版。
• tracker1从个人经验出发，强调在家庭服务器和小型项目中，使用Linux和Docker能快速搭建和迁移，减少了管理复杂性。
• steeleduncan反驳了“复杂技术易失败”的观点，认为设计良好的复杂技术是可靠的，并指出许多对systemd的抱怨源于不愿学习新工具。
• csdvrx支持systemd，认为其提供了更好的功能，尤其是在需要复杂逻辑时。同时指出，许多人因为不愿学习新工具而拒绝使用systemd，导致问题。
• mycall对系统可靠性提出了技术性问题，质疑个体组件可靠性对整体系统可靠性的影响。
• npodbielski认为，尽管作者提出的某些观点有道理，但普通用户并不想花时间管理服务器，需要更简单的自托管解决方案，如一键部署和自动更新。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在systemd的优缺点、FreeBSD与Linux的管理便捷性和工具稳定性上。
• 一些评论者强调了个人偏好和技术需求对操作系统选择的影响，而另一些则讨论了技术进步带来的复杂性及其合理性。
• 自托管和简化服务器管理的呼声较高，特别是针对普通用户的需求。

data.title: Oracle attempt to hide cybersecurity incident from customers?
data.author: 2bluesc
data.article_summary: Oracle被指试图隐瞒其SaaS服务中的严重网络安全事件。3月21日，Bleeping Computer报道了黑客rose87168声称入侵了Oracle的*.oraclecloud.com服务。Oracle否认了这一 breach，称“没有客户数据泄露”。然而，黑客提供了访问Oracle系统的证据，包括登录其管理服务的权限，并发布了一个内部会议录音，显示Oracle员工讨论了密码库和客户系统被入侵的情况。多位Oracle客户确认数据被泄露。尽管Oracle试图删除证据并避免书面确认，但多个消息来源证实了这起安全事件。Oracle被批评未公开透明地处理此事，建议其应明确告知客户事件详情及应对措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oracle安全事件及公司应对方式引发的争议

不同观点：
• [legitster] 认为Oracle的客户选择该公司通常是因为企业高层的幕后交易，而不是因为其产品质量。用户对Oracle的此类事件并不感到意外或愤怒，因为客户没有其他选择。
• [nerdjon] 强调安全事件在近年已变得普遍，如果Oracle坦诚面对，事件可能很快被遗忘，但其强烈否认和不透明的态度使问题变得更严重，质疑其动机和诚信。
• [autoexec] 指出当前州法律对数据泄露通知的要求缺乏执行力，呼吁需要更具威慑力的联邦法律来规范公司行为。
• [prdonahue] 分享了其与Oracle销售代表的沟通，Oracle方面否认了任何云客户数据泄露，但未提供详细说明。
• [mentalgear] 将此事件与Oracle创始人Larry Ellison的其他丑闻联系起来，认为这是其一贯作风。
• [islanderfun] 认为Oracle的当前行为符合“后真相时代”的特点，并指出这是Oracle长期以来的标准操作。
• [homiedk] 关注的是Oracle在安全事件中的技术控制缺失，如缺乏网络监控和安全响应机制，导致无法及时发现和阻止攻击。
• [tmpz22] 认为Oracle应依靠其良好声誉，向长期忠诚客户请求原谅。
• [layman51] 提到Oracle有能力删除Archive.org上的内容，暗示其影响力令人担忧。
• [richwater] 认为Oracle的行为符合其一贯预期，但对尚未涉及企业合同感到惊讶。
• [NickC25] 质疑Oracle是否构成证券欺诈，认为公司有法律义务告知投资者此类事件。
• [xyst] 认为Oracle故意掩盖其无能，主张这种欺骗公众和付费客户的行为应受到刑事处罚，并呼吁高管承担法律责任。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Oracle对安全事件的否认态度和信息不透明，以及公司是否应对客户和公众承担更多责任。
• 讨论中多次提到Oracle的声誉和过往行为，表明该公司在处理安全事件上的历史可能影响了公众的看法。
• 法律和监管问题也被提及，特别是关于公司是否应因不披露安全事件而受到更严厉的惩罚。

43535953.article_content:
Oracle attempt to hide serious cybersecurity incident from customers in Oracle SaaS service
Kevin Beaumont
·
Follow
Published in
DoublePulsar
·
4 min read
·
1 day ago
--
6
Listen
Share
Being a provider of cloud SaaS (Software-as-a-service) solutions requires certain cybersecurity responsibilities — including being transparent and open. The moment where this is tested at Oracle has arrived, as they have a serious cybersecurity incident playing out in a service they manage for customers.
Back on March 21st, Bleeping Computer ran a story around a threat actor named rose87168 claiming to have breached some Oracle services inside *.oraclecloud.com
Oracle
told
Bleeping Computer, and customers, “There has been no breach of Oracle Cloud. The published credentials are not for the Oracle Cloud. No Oracle Cloud customers experienced a breach or lost any data”
The threat actor then posted an archive.org URL and provided it to Bleeping Computer, strongly suggesting they had write access to login.us2.oraclecloud.com, a service using Oracle Access Manager. This server is entirely managed by Oracle:
https://cyberplace.social/@GossiTheDog/114202395143978043
Oracle have since requested Archive.org take down the proof:
The threat actor then provided a several hour long recording of an internal Oracle meeting, complete with Oracle employees talking for two hours:
The meeting is viewable
here
and the transcript is here:
https://github.com/j-klawson/oracle_breach_2025/blob/main/youtube_video_transcript.txt
The two hour video includes things like accessing internal Oracle password vaults, and customer facing systems:
I’ve masked the root passwords of Oracle’s systems
Both Hudson Rock and Bleeping Computer were then able to confirm with Oracle customers that their data — including staff email addresses — was in data released by the threat actor:
Oracle customers confirm data stolen in alleged cloud breach is valid
Despite Oracle denying a breach of its Oracle Cloud federated SSO login servers and the theft of account data for 6…
www.bleepingcomputer.com
The threat actor, rose87168, is still active online and releasing data — and threatening to release more:
They have also released data to cybersecurity threat intelligence providers.
In data released to a journalist for validation, it has now become 100% clear to me that there has been cybersecurity incident at Oracle, involving systems which processed customer data.
For example, the threat actor has publicly provided complete Oracle configuration files — current, too. As one example, they have provided Oracle webserver configuration files:
All the systems impacted are directly managed by Oracle. Some of the data provided to journalists is current, too. This is a serious cybersecurity incident which impacts customers, in a platform managed by Oracle.
Oracle are attempting to wordsmith statements around Oracle Cloud and use very specific words to avoid responsibility.
This is not okay.
Oracle need to clearly, openly and publicly communicate what happened, how it impacts customers, and what they’re doing about it. This is a matter of trust and responsibility. Step up, Oracle — or customers should start stepping off.

— Oracle rebadged old Oracle Cloud services to be Oracle Classic. Oracle Classic has the security incident.
Oracle are denying it on “Oracle Cloud” by using this scope — but it’s still Oracle cloud services that Oracle manage. That’s part of the wordplay.

data.title: A 6-Hour Time-Stretched Version of Brian Eno's Music for Airports
data.author: vinhnx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了布莱恩·伊诺（Brian Eno）的经典环境音乐专辑《机场音乐》（Music for Airports）。该专辑于1978年创作，旨在通过缓慢、冥想的音乐让听众接受死亡的自然性。专辑使用了数秒长的磁带循环，打破了传统的大小调音阶，探索了背景音的运用。虽然最初为私人使用而作，但后来在多个机场和音乐会上演出。2025年，一位YouTube用户创建了6小时的延展版，让音乐更加无缝和冥想。文章还提到环境音乐在公共空间的潜在应用，并呼吁支持开放文化的教育使命。读者评论则讨论了在不同场景中使用舒缓音乐的必要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Brian Eno的 ambient 音乐及其影响和相关作品的讨论

不同观点：
• [okeuro49] 引用了Brian Eno对机场背景音乐的思考，认为机场等场所的音乐不应只是无意义的背景音，而应与空间氛围契合，甚至反映出乘客面对飞行风险时的心理状态。
• [jquaint] 推荐了一个名为paulstretch的音频处理工具，可以用于制作类似Enos的 ambient 音乐，并分享了一个应用实例。
• [tquinn] 提到了电影《Heat》的背景音乐，认为它也是适合工作时听的 ambient 音乐，展示了对类似类型音乐的个人偏好。
• [matteason] 分享了一个互动式的 ambient 音景网页应用Ambiphone，并提供了应用示例和当前的开发状态。
• [morsch] 提出了自己更喜欢The Black Dog的Music for Real Airports，认为其与Eno的风格类似但更符合个人口味。

补充讨论：
• [ocal5] 和 [Lutzb] 提到了Brian Eno创作的Windows 95启动音乐，并分享了其慢速版本链接，扩展了Eno作品的范围。
• [curiousigor] 指出了访问某些网站时可能遇到的地区锁定问题，虽然没有具体结论，但提出了技术上的挑战。
• [bevan] 分享了一部关于Eno的纪录片，强调其与Eno的生成式音乐理念的关联。
• [ddxv] 推荐了Stars of the Lkd的音乐，为寻找类似氛围音乐的人提供了更多选择。
• [andyjohnson0] 表达了对Bang On A Can版本的偏爱，尽管其并非Eno的原作，展示了不同版本作品之间的比较。
• [CompoundEyes] 提到Steve Roach的“Structures from Silence”，通过音乐背后的故事（濒死体验）进一步探讨了音乐与生命脆弱性的关联。
• [chaosprint] 认为paulstretch工具可以广泛应用于各种音乐，以创造类似的ambient效果，扩展了工具的适用范围。
• [cage433] 推荐了Igor Levit演奏的Satie's Vexations，为那些觉得Eno音乐过短的人提供了更长的选择。
• [kryptonomist] 简单提及了某位适合深夜编码时听的音乐家，但没有具体展开。

争议焦点：
- 不同用户对ambient音乐的偏好和推荐不同作品，体现了主观审美差异。
- 对特定工具（如paulstretch）和音乐版本（如Bang On A Can vs. 原版）的偏好也展示了个人选择的多样性。

A 6‑Hour Time-Stretched Version of Brian Eno’s
Music For Airports
: Meditate, Relax, Study
in
Music
|   	March 17th, 2025
3 Comments
Writ­ing in his 1995 diary about his sem­i­nal ambi­ent album
Music for Air­ports
, Eno remem­bered his ini­tial thoughts going into it: “I want to make a kind of music that pre­pares you for dying–that doesn’t get all bright and cheer­ful and pre­tend you’re not a lit­tle appre­hen­sive, but which makes you say to your­self, ‘Actu­al­ly, it’s not that big a deal if I die.’”
Cre­at­ed in 1978 from sec­onds-long tape loops from a much longer improv ses­sion with musi­cians includ­ing Robert Wyatt,
Music for Air­ports
start­ed the idea of slow, med­i­ta­tive music that aban­doned typ­i­cal major and minor scales, brought in melod­ic ambi­gu­i­ty, and began the explo­ration of sounds that were designed to exist some­where in the back­ground, beyond the scope of full atten­tion.
For those who think 50 min­utes is too short and those piano notes too rec­og­niz­able, may we sug­gest this 6‑hour, time-stretched ver­sion of the album, cre­at­ed by YouTube user “Slow Motion TV.” The tonal field is the same, but now the notes are no attack, all decay. It’s gran­u­lar as hell, but you could imag­ine the whole piece unspool­ing unno­ticed in a ter­mi­nal while a flight is delayed for the third time. (Maybe that’s when the accep­tance of death hap­pens, when you’ve giv­en up on ever get­ting home?)
Unlike
Music for Films
, which fea­tured sev­er­al tracks Eno had giv­en to film­mak­ers like Derek Jar­man, it took some time for
Music for Air­ports
to be real­ized in its intend­ed loca­tion: being piped in at a ter­mi­nal at La Guardia, New York, some­time in the 1980s. And that was just a one-time thing.
?si=6VMY_yEfZdFDZbp6
The album seemed des­tined for per­son­al use only, but then in 1997 the mod­ern ensem­ble Bang on a Can played it live, trans­lat­ing the ran­dom­ness of out-of-sync tape loops into music nota­tion. Over the years they’ve per­formed it at air­ports in Brus­sels, the Nether­lands and Liv­er­pool, and in 2015 the group brought it to Ter­mi­nal 2 of San Diego Inter­na­tion­al.
Writ­ing for KCET, Alex Zaragoza report­ed
that “cry­ing babies, echoes of rolling suit­cas­es and board­ing pass­es serv­ing as tick­ets to the con­cert failed to remind any­one that they were, indeed, at one of the busiest air­ports in the coun­try. Even the tell­tale announce­ments were there:
Air­port secu­ri­ty is every­one’s respon­si­bil­i­ty. Do not leave bags unat­tend­ed
.”
And then in 2018,
Lon­don City Air­port played the orig­i­nal album
in a day-long loop for the album’s 40th anniver­sary.
As site-spe­cif­ic mul­ti-media art builds pop­u­lar­i­ty in the 21st cen­tu­ry with increas­ing­ly cheap­er and small­er tech­nol­o­gy, we might hope to hear ambi­ent drones, and not clas­sic rock or pop, in more and more land­scapes.
Note: An ear­li­er ver­sion of this post appeared on our site in 2019.

data.title: Where does air pollution come from?
data.author: kamaraju
data.article_summary: 每年数百万人因空气污染过早死亡。自人类开始燃烧材料作为燃料起，这一问题就已存在，从最初的木材和生物质到后来的化石燃料。然而，这是一个我们可以取得进展的环境和公共健康问题，因为全球已在减少空气污染物方面取得成功，许多曾经高度污染的国家如今空气已变得更清洁。为了有效应对空气污染，我们需要了解其来源。本文使用社区排放数据系统（CEDS）提供的长期全球和国家数据，该数据可追溯至18世纪，并定期更新至2022年。CEDS数据通过模型计算得出，具有一定不确定性，但为我们提供了全球排放趋势的合理一致的数据集。本文重点分析污染物来源，并按CEDS的分类进行细分，包括农业、建筑、能源、工业、交通和废物等类别。空气污染通过直接暴露和颗粒物形成等方式损害健康，导致大量过早死亡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：空气污染的成因、影响、监管及测量问题

不同观点：
• alexmccain6：认为空气污染的影响是隐性但广泛的，特别是对公共健康的长远影响。同时，对国际监管压力（如IMO 2020）如何促使航运业减少SO₂排放表示关注，并质疑是全球协调和监控的作用更大，还是因为替代方案的经济可行性更高。
• dynm：提出一个令人意外的污染源，即海浪飞沫（sea spray），认为其对沿海地区的PM2.5有显著贡献，但具体数据难以获取。
• xlii：对污染监测的实际执行表示怀疑，提到一些小镇存在污染但未被监测到，且地方当局反对安装传感器。质疑全球的环保努力是否对小规模污染者有效，尤其是与大型污染者对比时。
• sebastiennight：认为城市中的“煤烟”污染部分来源于汽车轮胎的磨损，而不仅仅是燃烧排放。
• TimByte：指出许多污染物都源自燃烧过程，无论是化石燃料还是农业副产品，本质上都是不同形式的燃烧和分解。
• pjsousa79：通过数据指出空气污染对低收入国家儿童健康的影响尤为严重，列举了多个国家因空气污染导致五岁以下儿童死亡的数据。
• johnthesecure：对空气污染导致的死亡数据持怀疑态度，认为许多死者即使没有污染也可能因其他原因死亡，建议讨论生活质量年（QUALYs）的损失可能更有意义。
• OsrsNeedsf2P：建议使用人均死亡率而不是绝对死亡数进行国家间比较，以便更准确地反映各国污染影响。
• nomilk：质疑城市空气质量监测数据的准确性，认为监测点的位置可能导致数据偏差，提出微环境对个人实际空气质量体验的影响更大。
• phtrivier：对航运业如何接受并遵守燃料更换规定表示好奇，质疑是替代燃料的经济性，还是行业受到某种强制或标准变更的影响。
• PeterStuer：批评一些国家通过将污染产业转移到其他国家来实现“绿色”和“净零排放”，实际上并未真正减少全球污染。
• kpmcc：对文章中使用的交互图表表示兴趣，询问所用的绘图库。
• h1fra：担心农业相关的污染（如氨和甲烷）没有减少的迹象，认为改变全球70亿人的饮食习惯几乎不可能。
• spwa4：希望文章能更多关注已取得的环保进展，例如过去使用含铅汽油造成的损害比现在的NOx问题严重得多。

补充讨论：

Home
Air Pollution
Millions of people
die prematurely
from air pollution every year.
This problem has existed
since humans started burning materials for fuel — first wood and biomass, then fossil fuels.
But it’s an environmental and public health problem that we can make progress on. We know this because the world
has already
been successful
in reducing air pollutants, and many countries that used to be highly polluted now have much cleaner air than they used to.
To tackle air pollution effectively — to focus our efforts on the interventions that will have the biggest impact — we need to understand where it’s coming from.
That’s why we wrote this article.
1
A note on data and definitions
The main data source we rely on is the Community Emissions Data System (CEDS). There are a couple of reasons why we think it’s an incredibly valuable resource:
It has long-term global and national data extending back to the 18th century and is frequently updated with the latest estimates for 2022.
It’s published with an open-access license and transparent methodology and inputs, which you can find
on GitHub
. The peer-reviewed paper describing the methodology is
here
.
2
This online data resource is open to user comments and feedback, so errors or issues can be easily reported.
CEDS provides clear documentation of data improvements and detailed comparisons of recent updates against previous versions.
To be clear, CEDS does not have high-quality
measurements
of emissions of air pollutants — certainly not dating back to the 18th century. These figures are calculated and modeled based on inputs, such as the quantity of different fuels that were burned, technological advancements and pollution controls, fertilizer use, and agricultural production. You can, for example, estimate the amount of sulfur dioxide produced from burning one tonne of coal in a power plant (with or without pollution filters).
Of course, this means the data comes with some uncertainty, especially in earlier periods. However, it gives us a reasonable and consistent global dataset to understand how trends in emissions of air pollutants have changed over time.

43553663.article_summary: 每年数百万人因空气污染过早死亡。自人类开始燃烧材料作为燃料起，这一问题就已存在，从最初的木材和生物质到后来的化石燃料。然而，这是一个我们可以取得进展的环境和公共健康问题，因为全球已在减少空气污染物方面取得成功，许多曾经高度污染的国家如今空气已变得更清洁。为了有效应对空气污染，我们需要了解其来源。本文使用社区排放数据系统（CEDS）提供的长期全球和国家数据，该数据可追溯至18世纪，并定期更新至2022年。CEDS数据通过模型计算得出，具有一定不确定性，但为我们提供了全球排放趋势的合理一致的数据集。本文重点分析污染物来源，并按CEDS的分类进行细分，包括农业、建筑、能源、工业、交通和废物等类别。空气污染通过直接暴露和颗粒物形成等方式损害健康，导致大量过早死亡。

主要讨论点：AI工具在代码调试、软件开发以及其他领域（如食谱生成、语音控制）中的应用和潜力

不同观点：
• **jumploops** 认为，虽然Claude Code在处理独立软件问题时最终能解决问题，但在调试困难问题时，o1 Pro表现更为出色。他提到在与同事对比测试中，o1 Pro能一次性解决问题，而Claude Code需要多次迭代。尽管最终完成时间相近，但o1 Pro帮助解决了Claude未发现的问题。
  
• **nine_k** 对自动化工具在非技术人员中的应用持怀疑态度，认为不仅需要AI具备编码能力，还需要其具备架构和高级软件工程师的能力，才能让非技术人员有效使用。特别指出，要让非技术人员理解如日志跟踪和版本控制等概念是一个重大挑战。
  
• **osigurdson** 表示，目前Windsurf与Claude的实用性有限，虽然未来可能会有突破，但目前主要用途在于教学而非实际编码。他认为ChatGPT在当前阶段作为AI编辑器已经足够。

• **iambateman** 关注自动化系统在维护项目中的上下文理解能力，提出如果大量代码被误操作（如3k LOC被重复），AI系统能否理解并修复。他预测未来可能会出现LLM意外重新实现整个功能的新型错误。

补充讨论：
• **apgwoz** 和 **ttd** 对食谱网站的生成内容提出质疑和批评，前者因过敏反应而愤怒，后者对食谱中的奇怪食材表示嘲讽。
  
• **Yiling-J** 推荐了自己的工具tablepilot，用于生成大量食谱，表明AI在特定任务中已有实际应用。
  
• **peterldowns** 和 **low_tech_love** 对项目的语音控制和区块链结合等创新点表示赞赏，认为这是技术的前沿应用。

• **Retr0id** 和 **DidYaWipe** 则关注用户体验问题，如界面错误和术语不清晰，表明项目在实际应用中仍有改进空间。

• **tombert** 分享了使用Conjure插件在Clojure中的积极体验，认为这种即时执行和反馈的编码方式改变了编码习惯，并对Rust中缺乏类似功能表示遗憾。

争议焦点：
• AI工具在调试和代码生成中的实际效果和应用场景。
• 非技术人员能否通过AI工具有效参与软件开发。
• 自动化系统在处理复杂代码问题时的可靠性和潜在错误。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者计划将一个简单的脚踏卡丁车改造成一辆电动汽车的过程。改造目标包括使用电动马达、保持小尺寸以便运输、具备足够的动力和安全性，并能应对各种地形。作者设定了两个驾驶模式：手动模式和遥控模式，以确保安全。卡丁车的底盘选用了一辆二手脚踏卡丁车，并加装了MDF木板以增强结构。马达来自废弃的平衡车，具备强劲的动力和紧凑的设计。电池选用36V、10Ah的型号，并安装了放电保护系统和电量显示屏。此外，还使用电压转换器为电子设备和灯光提供不同电压。整个项目旨在为作者的孩子打造一辆既安全又有趣的电动卡丁车。
